chain_focus: AI-enabled drug discovery, precision medicine, autonomous laboratories, and the omics data platforms that feed biological models. The chain follows compute and cloud infrastructure into scientific software and AI-native discovery platforms, then into diagnostics, drug programs, and named biopharma customers.

players.product: AI-enabled molecular discovery programs

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Chris Boerner said that over the past several years 'BMS has embedded AI across its research and enterprise operations, demand for compute has grown alongside the scale and maturity of our AI capabilities.' In support of that expansion BMS 'recently announced partnership agreements with both Anthropic and NVIDIA.' Management said this will concretely help its scientists do three things: 'understand disease biology more deeply, design and test candidate molecules faster, and make earlier, better-informed decisions about which programs to move forward.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: AI is also being applied to clinical-development execution. Chief Medical Officer Cristian Massacesi said BMS now identifies and mitigates execution risk across every ongoing study - study design, statistical assumptions and comparator-arm performance - and described the work as 'integrating AI technology, data, and everything to have for each program this PTS improvement.' Separately, the 120 mg admilparant dose added to the phase III program was selected on the basis of 'modeling work, showing that there was a dose relation.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline productivity: management said the differentiated pipeline has 'the potential to introduce more than 10 new medicines by the end of the decade,' including iberdomide and mezigdomide, plus 'over 30 meaningful lifecycle management opportunities during that same period.' Ten products in the overall portfolio achieved double-digit growth in the quarter, and management said it continues to expect pivotal readouts across its therapeutic areas by the end of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: >10 new medicines by end of decade; >30 lifecycle management opportunities; 10 products with double-digit growth

quarterly_data.signal: Total revenue in the second quarter increased 5% year-over-year to approximately $13 billion. Growth portfolio revenue rose 14% to $7.6 billion, now representing nearly 60% of total revenue, with REBLOZYL up 29%, BREYANZI up 41%, CAMZYOS up 59% to $416 million and COBENFY up 81% to $63 million. ELIQUIS revenue was approximately $4.5 billion, up 21%. Gross margin was 71.4%, operating expenses were $4.1 billion, the effective tax rate was 16.5% and diluted earnings per share were $2.04.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$13B (+5%); growth portfolio $7.6B (+14%), ~60% of total; ELIQUIS ~$4.5B (+21%); gross margin 71.4%; opex $4.1B; EPS $2.04

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue and adjusted diluted EPS was increased on first-half results, while maintaining projections for gross margin, other income and expense, and the tax rate. The revision incorporates projected ELIQUIS revenue growth of 20%-25% and a less pronounced total legacy portfolio revenue decrease now expected to be between 4% and 6%; operating expenses were raised slightly for accelerated pre-launch activities supporting the CELMoDs iberdomide and mezigdomide. Cash equivalents and marketable securities were approximately $11.5 billion, the company generated approximately $3.4 billion in operating cash flow and paid down an additional $1.2 billion in debt.
quarterly_data.figure: ELIQUIS growth 20%-25%; legacy portfolio decline 4%-6%; cash ~$11.5B; operating cash flow ~$3.4B; debt repaid $1.2B

quarterly_data.signal: Upcoming catalysts: BMS now expects the milvexian atrial fibrillation study to read out in the first quarter of 2027, and management disclosed the study needs to recruit 430 events for the primary endpoint of strokes and systemic embolisms and 530 events for bleedings before database lock. Admilparant in IPF is guided to read out by the end of this year with PPF a few months later, iberdomide has an August 17th PDUFA date, mezigdomide a May 13th, 2027 PDUFA date and CAMZYOS in adolescents a September 30th PDUFA date; COBENFY ADEPT top-line readouts now begin in early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: milvexian Afib readout Q1 2027; 430 primary events and 530 bleeding events required; iberdomide PDUFA August 17th; mezigdomide PDUFA May 13th, 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Growth versus legacy split. CFO David Elkins said growth portfolio revenue rose 14% while within the legacy portfolio 'ELIQUIS delivered demand-driven growth of 21%, which nearly offset declines from generic entry across the remainder of the legacy portfolio.' He added that 'despite full generic availability in the U.S., REVLIMID revenue remains more resilient.' CEO Chris Boerner framed the quarter as progress 'towards transitioning the portfolio to fuel durable long-term growth.'
quarterly_data.figure: growth portfolio +14%; ELIQUIS demand-driven growth of 21%

quarterly_data.signal: OPDIVO revenue decreased 4% to approximately $2.5 billion, 'primarily driven by continued conversion to OPDIVO Qvantig in the U.S.,' David Elkins said, adding that 'in the quarter, we saw some inventory build at the wholesale level, reversing some of the drawdown we referenced in the first quarter.' On the subcutaneous product he said in prepared remarks that it 'continued its strong launch trajectory with revenue of $261 million and is now annualizing at over $1 billion' (the transcript prints the brand name as Sotyktu at that point in the oncology section), and in Q&A that 'now we have 15% share, so well on our way to that 30%-40%,' concluding that taking Opdivo Qvantig and Opdivo together 'we're really pleased with the progress of that franchise.'
quarterly_data.figure: OPDIVO -4% to approximately $2.5 billion; subcutaneous launch revenue $261 million, annualizing at over $1 billion; 15% share versus a 30%-40% target

quarterly_data.signal: OPDUALAG 'delivered another quarter of strong double-digit growth, which continues to be driven by demand globally and its leading position as a standard of care in first-line melanoma in the U.S.,' David Elkins said. Quantifying the growth portfolio in Q&A he said 'Opdualag was up 22%, REVLIMID 29%, BREYANZI, we continue to see great growth there at 41%, and CAMZYOS was at 59%.'
quarterly_data.figure: OPDUALAG +22%

quarterly_data.signal: REBLOZYL grew 29%, which David Elkins attributed to 'solid uptake in first-line MDS-associated anemia, continued strength in the second-line setting, and further penetration in the first-line Rh-negative population.'
quarterly_data.figure: REBLOZYL +29%

quarterly_data.signal: BREYANZI posted 41% growth, 'driven by its best-in-class profile and strong demand across approved indications in both the U.S. and international markets,' David Elkins said, while flagging a sequential headwind: 'as in prior years, we anticipate the typical summer demand patterns to moderate growth in the third quarter.'
quarterly_data.figure: BREYANZI +41%; growth expected to moderate in the third quarter on typical summer demand patterns

quarterly_data.signal: ELIQUIS second-half dynamics. David Elkins said revenue of approximately $4.5 billion, up 21%, was 'driven by strong demand through continued market share gains,' and that as a result of the price decrease implemented at the start of the year 'U.S. second-half sales are expected to benefit from the elimination of the accumulated CPI penalty in certain government channels.' Chief Commercialization Officer Adam Lenkowsky said U.S. new to brand share 'is approaching 80%' and that the WAC reduction taken January 1st means second-half U.S. sales will be higher than first-half sales, with full-year growth of roughly 20%-25%.
quarterly_data.figure: ELIQUIS approximately $4.5 billion, +21%; U.S. new to brand share approaching 80%; full-year growth roughly 20%-25%

quarterly_data.signal: ELIQUIS beyond 2026. Adam Lenkowsky said BMS 'still expect the $1.5 billion-$2 billion step down in 2027 that we referenced on the Q1 call,' with U.S. sales carrying forward into next year 'offset by the patent expiry of ELIQUIS in Europe in mid Q4.' He also said the ELIQUIS loss of exclusivity 'is April of 2028, and this lines up very nicely with the filing and launch timelines of milvexian,' adding 'we expect that ELIQUIS LOE to lead directly into the successful launch of milvexian.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 step down of $1.5 billion-$2 billion; Europe patent expiry mid Q4; U.S. loss of exclusivity April of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CAMZYOS revenues increased 59% to $416 million, 'reflecting continued promotional efforts, new patient prescriber additions, and deeper penetration into the community setting,' David Elkins said. Chris Boerner said the FDA accepted the supplemental NDA for CAMZYOS in adolescents with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and that BMS continues to 'actively plan our previously announced phase III study evaluating CAMZYOS in patients with non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and expect to initiate the study by the end of the year.'
quarterly_data.figure: CAMZYOS +59% to $416 million

quarterly_data.signal: Sotyktu global revenue grew 23%. David Elkins said BMS is 'supporting the recent indication for psoriatic arthritis in adults' and looking to the phase III lupus readouts later this year. Adam Lenkowsky said the SLE readout comes this year and Sjogren's next year, that the phase II study 'was one of the largest and most compelling in SLE to date, having met both the primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints,' and that BMS can differentiate on overall clinical responses, efficacy in skin and joint involvement, reduced steroid dependence and associated toxicity. Cristian Massacesi added that patient demographics, disease characteristics, trial management and endpoints in the phase III studies closely mirror the phase II.
quarterly_data.figure: Sotyktu +23% globally

quarterly_data.signal: COBENFY grew 81% to $63 million, 'reflecting continued steady progress in the schizophrenia market.' Adam Lenkowsky said the brand saw 'roughly a 15% growth in TRx quarter-over-quarter' with consistent increases in new prescribers, while BMS still needs to 'accelerate new patient starts as well as improve repeat prescribing' in a disease state where prescribing behavior is 'deeply entrenched.' On dosing, he said BMS has been educating physicians on rapidly titrating to the effective dose of 125 ml 'as we see far too many patients that remain on either the 50 ml or 100 ml dose,' and that 125 ml prescribing has increased since the phase IV SWITCH study was introduced.
quarterly_data.figure: COBENFY +81% to $63 million; TRx +15% quarter-over-quarter

quarterly_data.signal: COBENFY Alzheimer's psychosis program detail. Chief Medical Officer Cristian Massacesi said ADEPT-1 is event-driven with psychotic relapses accruing more slowly than predicted, and that 'ADEPT 1 will be the first interim analysis to read out by the end of this year or beginning of next year,' while ADEPT-2 and ADEPT-4 enrollment was slowed by scrutiny over patient and trial quality, with measures now implemented to accelerate enrollment. BMS will share safety and efficacy data later this year from the open label lead-in portion of ADEPT-1 and from ADEPT-3, the open label rollover study for patients who already completed ADEPT-1, -2 and -4. The phase III BALSAM-1 and BALSAM-2 studies of COBENFY in bipolar I disorder 'continue to enroll well' and are anticipated to read out in the first half of 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: ADEPT-1 first interim analysis by the end of this year or beginning of next year; BALSAM-1 and BALSAM-2 readouts in the first half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Milvexian commercial setup. Adam Lenkowsky said atrial fibrillation is 'a very large market' with 'approximately 10 million patients diagnosed and treated in the U.S.,' and that even with ELIQUIS 'there's still roughly 40% of patients who should be anticoagulated who are undertreated, underdosed, or discontinue treatment,' driven largely by physician concerns around bleeding risk. He said the ELIQUIS infrastructure built over many years already covers 'virtually all of the physicians in atrial fibrillation,' with the existing Zeposia team able to cover the small number of stroke neurologists, so 'we really have the full infrastructure commercially set.' Chris Boerner said 'there would be no constraints with respect to the relationship that we have with Pfizer in terms of our ability to successfully launch and commercialize milvexian.'
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 10 million diagnosed and treated Afib patients in the U.S.; roughly 40% of patients who should be anticoagulated are undertreated, underdosed or discontinue

quarterly_data.signal: Admilparant market opportunity. Adam Lenkowsky said IPF is 'a roughly $4 billion market' that BMS expects to grow significantly and that 'could maybe double to $8 billion-$10 billion by the middle of the 2030s with improved treatment options.' He said '50%-60% of IPF patients continue to stop their medications by 12 months' on current standard of care, and that recently approved agents carry 'an overall rate of diarrhea of 40%, over 60% in combination,' whereas admilparant's phase II side effect profile 'is comparable to placebo.' A second-line add-on and switch market is emerging for the first time, with 'over 50% of new Jascayd starts are coming after generic Ofev or generic Esbriet as switch or add-on treatments.'
quarterly_data.figure: IPF market roughly $4 billion, potentially $8 billion-$10 billion by the middle of the 2030s; 50%-60% of patients stop medication by 12 months; diarrhea rate 40%, over 60% in combination; over 50% of Jascayd starts post-generic

quarterly_data.signal: Admilparant phase III design. Cristian Massacesi said the LPA1 antagonist is tested at two doses, '60 mg, it is the dose that emerged from the phase II, but also 120 mg that was introduced later,' giving BMS 'two shots on goal in each of the studies, IPF and PPF,' with the studies 'fully powered for both doses.' The higher dose was added on modeling work showing a dose relation and was cleared by the independent data monitoring committee after a randomized run-in; recruitment is complete and the blinded safety profile on hypotension has been 'very reassuring.' He said the PPF readout will come 'just a few months after' IPF, 'very same ballpark timelines beginning next year,' and described LPA1 as novel because it works on the fibrotic and inflammatory pathway and potentially on the epithelium repair pathway.
quarterly_data.figure: two doses, 60 mg and 120 mg; PPF readout a few months after the IPF readout, beginning next year

quarterly_data.signal: CELMoD launch preparation. Adam Lenkowsky said the iberdomide PDUFA date is 'just a few weeks away' and commercial teams are launch-ready, with mezigdomide's PDUFA 'in May of next year.' He said '70%-80% of patients are treated with multiple myeloma in the community,' where the oral CELMoDs fit the workflow of the practice, and that iberdomide 'will replace Pomalyst and REVLIMID in the leading triplet regimens in second-line and combined with daratumumab.' Progression-free survival data 'should be available within just a few months after our approval, which will certainly help accelerate uptake.' Golcadomide would be the third CELMoD in the market, targeting first-line LBCL and second-line follicular lymphoma.
quarterly_data.figure: 70%-80% of multiple myeloma patients treated in the community

quarterly_data.signal: Oncology pipeline progress shown at ASCO in June. Chris Boerner cited positive phase III data from the mezigdomide SUCCESSOR-2 study in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma showing 'a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival,' and encouraging phase III data from two iza-bren studies in difficult-to-treat solid tumors. BMS is initiating a fourth global phase III study in first-line EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer, shared encouraging early phase II global data for pemetrexed in combination with chemotherapy in first-line non-small cell lung cancer, and is initiating a new phase II study combining pemetrexed with imzokitug, its CCR8 antibody. Cristian Massacesi pointed to the internal BCL6 degrader from the protein targeted degradation platform as a transcription factor target that could not be inhibited but can be degraded.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Neuroscience pipeline. Cristian Massacesi said the anti-tau antibody moponitat is 'a very potential best-in-class' antibody binding the R1 and R3 domains of the microtubule binding region, the critical area that leads to formation and spread of tau tangles. The phase I was 'very reassuring in terms of the safety and tolerability of the product,' phase II recruitment is complete and the readout is due next year, assessing tau clearance plus endpoints related to cognition and potential overall clinical benefit. He said a second mechanism is now validated, tau on top of amyloid, and that BMS is building its Alzheimer's portfolio and developing next generation assets that are 'shuttles to increase the brain penetration.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Capital allocation and business development. David Elkins said business development 'remains a priority, and we are regularly evaluating opportunities in the therapeutic areas we know best while continuing to return cash to shareholders through our commitment to the dividend.' Chris Boerner said BD 'continues to be a top allocation priority' but that with a strong late-stage pipeline 'we certainly don't feel any compulsion to chase deals'; the criteria are therapeutic areas BMS knows well, areas where the science is compelling and a compelling financial case, ideally deals that de-risk the near-term growth profile, and BMS has 'the financial flexibility and the capabilities to be in the mix.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Cost discipline and productivity. Chris Boerner said 'our focus on productivity continues to generate meaningful savings,' which combined with strong free cash flow generation and the balance sheet 'continue to fortify the company's financial foundation.' David Elkins said second quarter operating expenses of $4.1 billion continue to benefit from the strategic productivity initiative, which provides 'both the ability to reduce expenses in identified areas, as well as the flexibility to invest in multiple growth-oriented opportunities,' and that full-year operating expenses were raised slightly to account for accelerated pre-launch activities supporting the CELMoDs, 'the expanding pomalidomide development program, and opportunities to further support the growth portfolio.' Gross margin of 71.4% reflected product mix.
quarterly_data.figure: operating expenses $4.1 billion; gross margin 71.4%

quarterly_data.signal: The 10-K's table of late-stage developments lists the FDA and European Commission (EC) approvals BMS announced during 2025: FDA approval of Opdivo + Yervoy as a first-line treatment of unresectable or metastatic microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair deficient CRC (April 2025, more than two months ahead of the June 23, 2025 PDUFA goal date) and as a first-line treatment for unresectable or metastatic HCC (April 2025); FDA approval of Breyanzi for relapsed or refractory MZL (December 2025); FDA approval of label updates for Abecma and Breyanzi removing their REMS programs (June 2025); EC approvals of Augtyro for ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC and NTRK fusion solid tumors (February 2025), Opdivo + Yervoy for first-line unresectable or advanced HCC (March 2025), Breyanzi for relapsed or refractory FL (March 2025), Opdivo with platinum-based chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment followed by adjuvant Opdivo for resectable NSCLC (May 2025), Opdivo Qvantig subcutaneous injection across most previously approved adult solid tumor Opdivo indications (May 2025) and Breyanzi for relapsed or refractory MCL (November 2025).
quarterly_data.figure: FDA: Opdivo + Yervoy CRC and HCC (April 2025), Breyanzi MZL (December 2025); EC: Augtyro (February 2025), Opdivo + Yervoy HCC and Breyanzi FL (March 2025), Opdivo NSCLC and Opdivo Qvantig (May 2025), Breyanzi MCL (November 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration (10-K XBRL): McKesson Corporation accounted for 36% of BMS's revenue in 2025 (34% in 2024, 33% in 2023), Cencora, Inc. for 29% (29%, 29%) and Cardinal Health, Inc. for 22% (22%, 23%). The 10-K adds that receivables from the three largest customers in the U.S. represented 75% of total trade receivables at December 31, 2025 (74% a year earlier).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue share: McKesson 36%, Cencora 29%, Cardinal Health 22%; three largest U.S. customers 75% of trade receivables

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 revenue per the 10-K was $48,194 million versus $48,300 million in 2024: the Growth Portfolio rose 17% to $26,409 million (Opdivo $10,049 million, Breyanzi $1,358 million up 82%, Camzyos $1,068 million up 77%) while the Legacy Portfolio fell 15% to $21,785 million (Eliquis $14,443 million up 8%, Revlimid $2,951 million down 49%).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue $48,194 million (2024: $48,300 million); Growth Portfolio $26,409 million (+17%); Legacy Portfolio $21,785 million (-15%)

quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing and capex per the 10-K: annual capital expenditures were approximately $1.3 billion in 2025 ($1.2 billion in 2024) and are expected to be approximately $1.3 billion in 2026, tied to expanding cell therapy and other manufacturing capabilities; over the next three years BMS plans investments to add U.S. domestic manufacturing capabilities. During 2025 it completed a new cell therapy manufacturing facility in Leiden, Netherlands and opened a new radiopharmaceutical facility in Indianapolis, Indiana; it relies on third parties for all or part of the active ingredient or drug substance of products including Eliquis, Opdivo, Yervoy and Camzyos and is expanding its use of third-party manufacturers, and it owns or leases facilities at approximately 130 sites worldwide.
quarterly_data.figure: capex approximately $1.3 billion (2025) and approximately $1.3 billion expected (2026); approximately 130 sites

quarterly_data.signal: The Q2 2026 earnings release's product and pipeline updates list two European Commission approvals: on June 1 the EC approved Opdivo in combination with doxorubicin, vinblastine and dacarbazine for adult and adolescent patients 12 years of age and older with previously untreated Stage III or IV classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (based on the Phase 3 SWOG 1826 study), and on May 8 the EC approved Sotyktu, alone or in combination with methotrexate, for psoriatic arthritis in adults with an inadequate response or intolerance to a prior disease-modifying antirheumatic therapy (based on POETYK PsA-1 and PsA-2).
quarterly_data.figure: EC approvals: Opdivo cHL (June 1), Sotyktu PsA (May 8)

quarterly_data.signal: The Q2 2026 earnings release gives the raised 2026 non-GAAP guidance figures: total revenues approximately $49.0 billion to $50.0 billion (April guidance approximately $46.0 billion to $47.5 billion), reflecting broad-based and continuing momentum across the portfolio; operating expenses approximately $16.5 billion (previously approximately $16.3 billion) due to increased investment behind key pipeline programs and new product launches; diluted EPS $6.75 - $7.00 (previously $6.05 - $6.35); gross margin approximately 69% - 70%, other income/(expense) approximately ($700 million) and a tax rate of approximately 18% unchanged.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue ~$49.0-$50.0 billion (was ~$46.0-$47.5 billion); operating expenses ~$16.5 billion (was ~$16.3 billion); non-GAAP EPS $6.75-$7.00 (was $6.05-$6.35)

players.product: AI-enabled antibody and drug discovery programs

quarterly_data.signal: Biomarker-driven patient identification kept scaling in neuroscience and oncology. Management said the number of p-tau217 blood tests more than doubled compared to Q2 2025 and that this is translating to more people being diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and accessing treatment. On the LIBRETTO-432 adjuvant selpercatinib result, which reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 83% versus placebo, Chief Scientific and Product Officer Dan Skovronsky said the effect size 'underscores the importance of comprehensive biomarker tests across all stages of disease.'
quarterly_data.figure: p-tau217 blood tests more than doubled year over year; selpercatinib recurrence or death risk -83% versus placebo

quarterly_data.signal: Genetic-medicine capability advanced on both the science and the manufacturing side. In the phase I-B study of VERVE-102, a gene-editing program designed to inactivate the PCSK9 gene, a single infusion reduced PCSK9 by 88% and LDL cholesterol by 62% at the highest dose. Lilly also opened its first dedicated genetic medicine manufacturing facility in Lebanon, Indiana, and produced the first batch of commercial material at its new site in Limerick, Ireland.
quarterly_data.figure: PCSK9 -88%; LDL cholesterol -62% at the highest dose; first dedicated genetic medicine manufacturing facility opened

quarterly_data.signal: R&D expenses increased 14%, driven by continued investment in the pipeline, including more than 40 active phase III programs. Management said business development is an important component of the R&D strategy and that 'the pace and average deal size have also continued to increase,' with agreements announced in the quarter to acquire Curevo, LimmaTech Biologics and The Vaccine Company, the acquisition of AtaiBeckley, and the completed Centessa acquisition adding cleminorexton in phase II.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expense +14%; more than 40 active phase III programs

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue grew 48% compared to Q2 2025, with key products up almost $6.8 billion and the oncology, immunology and neuroscience medicines collectively growing 121%. MOUNJARO and ZEPBOUND combined for $14.9 billion of revenue and contributed $6.3 billion of growth. Gross margin was 86.3% of revenue, up approximately 1.3 percentage points, and non-GAAP performance margin was 54.8%, up nine percentage points.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue +48%; key products +$6.8B; oncology/immunology/neuroscience +121%; MOUNJARO+ZEPBOUND $14.9B (+$6.3B); gross margin 86.3%; performance margin 54.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Non-GAAP earnings per share were $8.38, including acquired IPR&D charges of $3.03, versus $6.31 in Q2 2025. Full-year guidance was raised: management increased the low-end of the revenue range by $3 billion and the high-end by $2 billion to $85 billion-$87 billion, with non-GAAP performance margin of 49%-50.5% and non-GAAP earnings per share of $35.50-$36.50.
quarterly_data.figure: EPS $8.38 (incl. $3.03 acquired IPR&D) vs $6.31; FY revenue $85B-$87B; performance margin 49%-50.5%; FY EPS $35.50-$36.50

quarterly_data.signal: Upcoming catalysts: with TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 complete, Lilly said it now has the clinical data package to support global registrations for retatrutide in obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain and plans to submit in the U.S. in quarter one 2027 under the BLA pathway. The first obstructive sleep apnea readout for Foundayo comes later this year, with an additional five ongoing phase III programs studying Foundayo, and EMBER-4 for INLURIYO is slated to read out next year in the adjuvant setting.
quarterly_data.figure: retatrutide U.S. submission Q1 2027; five additional ongoing Foundayo phase III programs

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Lucas Montarce gave the price, rate and volume split. U.S. revenue increased 33% in Q2, primarily driven by volume growth from ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO as well as contributions from the Immunology, Oncology and Neuroscience portfolio. U.S. price declined by 3%, driven by ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO; U.S. price in the quarter benefited from a change to estimates for rebates and discounts, and excluding those adjustments U.S. price declined by 9%.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. revenue +33%; U.S. price -3%, or -9% excluding the rebate and discount estimate adjustments

quarterly_data.signal: Ex-U.S. growth was broad based. Lucas Montarce said Europe revenue grew 55% in constant currency on sustained strong volume growth of MOUNJARO, and also benefited from a $250 million Jardiance milestone payment. Japan revenue grew 30% in constant currency driven by MOUNJARO and KISUNLA, China revenue grew 93% in constant currency on MOUNJARO uptake, and rest of world revenue grew 136% in constant currency driven by MOUNJARO, primarily in Latin America and Asia.
quarterly_data.figure: Europe +55% constant currency including a $250 million Jardiance milestone; Japan +30% cc; China +93% cc; rest of world +136% cc

quarterly_data.signal: Capital returns in the quarter. CEO Dave Ricks said Lilly distributed $1.5 billion in dividends in the second quarter and executed $1.6 billion in share repurchases.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.5 billion of dividends and $1.6 billion of share repurchases in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: Lucas Montarce sized the U.S. obesity market and Lilly's share of it. Total prescriptions in the U.S. incretin analog market grew 31% compared to Q2 2025. Within the U.S. incretin analogs obesity market, total prescriptions grew by 78% in Q2, and approximately six out of 10 total prescriptions and approximately seven out of 10 injectable prescriptions were for a Lilly medicine. Self-pay accounted for approximately 45% of total ZEPBOUND prescriptions in Q2 and approximately 55% of new prescriptions.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. incretin analog total prescriptions +31%; U.S. obesity incretin total prescriptions +78%; Lilly approximately six out of 10 total and seven out of 10 injectable prescriptions; ZEPBOUND self-pay approximately 45% of total and 55% of new prescriptions

quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. Type 2 diabetes incretin analogs market is the slower, more mature half of the franchise. Lucas Montarce said total prescriptions grew 9% compared to Q2 2025, reflecting a more mature market compared to obesity, and more than six out of 10 prescriptions for an incretin were for a Lilly medicine. He added that the early uptake of oral GLP-1s has been encouraging and is expanding the market of people taking incretin therapy, while injectable incretins continue to be an important growth driver and account for three out of four new patient starts.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. Type 2 diabetes incretin total prescriptions +9%; Lilly more than six out of 10 prescriptions; injectables account for three out of four new patient starts

quarterly_data.signal: The international incretin analogs market has increased by 74% since the same period last year, as measured by IQVIA gross sales. Lucas Montarce said Lilly is the global market leader and strengthened that position, gaining almost 2 percentage points of share compared to Q1 2026 to reach approximately 55%. MOUNJARO Q2 revenue growth was driven by China, Korea, Germany, the U.K. and Mexico, and MOUNJARO is now reimbursed for both Type 2 diabetes and obesity in France. He said market share leadership is already established, so market expansion will be key to driving sustainable growth.
quarterly_data.figure: international incretin analogs market +74% on IQVIA gross sales; Lilly share approximately 55%, up almost 2 percentage points versus Q1 2026

quarterly_data.signal: The Medicare access milestone is the single biggest change to the U.S. obesity addressable market this quarter. Dave Ricks said the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Program, reached in partnership with the U.S. government, launched on July 1 and grants 20 million eligible Americans insurance coverage for GLP-1s for obesity at a low out-of-pocket price of $50 per month, and that with this expansion 35% more people now have coverage for Lilly's obesity medicines in the United States. Ilya Yuffa put the figure at about 35% more Americans able to access obesity therapy, said Lilly is working closely with CMS on prior authorization criteria and stakeholder education, and said LillyDirect has been enabled to fulfill on the Bridge process.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 million eligible Americans; $50 per month out-of-pocket; access for about 35% more Americans

quarterly_data.signal: Early Bridge uptake skews injectable and new-to-therapy. Ilya Yuffa said there is a visible inflection point for both ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO over the last few weeks, partly driven by Bridge, with a significant preference towards injectable at probably around 80% of people getting treatment, and approximately 60%-70% of them new people who have not had access before.

He said the CVS access Lilly accomplished starts in Q4, that medical exceptions are a short-term driver Lilly expects to fade as open access broadens, and that the resulting price decline is very much embedded in the guide and will be more than offset by volume growth.
quarterly_data.figure: LillyDirect direct-to-patient $299 to $449; Bridge program $245; CVS access starting in Q4

quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. Foundayo (orforglipron) launch inflected in late July. Management secured commercial access across all three major PBMs in June, with CVS adding Foundayo in June, then began broad direct-to-consumer marketing. Ilya Yuffa said that in the last week of July Lilly is almost doubling the volume it had just a month ago, and that around one out of four new starts are on Foundayo. The prescriber base grew from the 8,000 cited on the prior earnings call to 36,000, with sampling covering the first 30 days of the first dose across the prescriber base and full supply to enable it. Marketing, selling and administrative expenses increased 25% as Lilly invested in promotional activities to support current and planned product launches.
quarterly_data.figure: prescribers 8,000 to 36,000; around one out of four new starts on Foundayo; volume almost doubled versus a month earlier; marketing, selling and administrative expenses +25%

Lilly launched in the UAE in early May, received approval in Saudi Arabia for obesity and in Mexico for obesity and Type 2 diabetes, and has the product under regulatory review in more than 40 additional markets with a global rollout in all major markets expected in 2027. Patrik Jonsson said most patients are naive to incretin treatment, that Lilly's combined incretin share held steady even with a second oral entering the UAE market, and that Lilly is extremely well-positioned in terms of supply with no gating of launches either.

quarterly_data.signal: In Immunology, Ebglyss (lebrikizumab) worldwide sales more than doubled compared to Q2 2025, and in the U.S. it continued to gain share of new prescriptions, increasing by approximately 4 percentage points in the specialty dermatology market since last year. The FDA approved a new maintenance dosing regimen of once every eight weeks in atopic dermatitis, giving patients the option of as few as six maintenance injections per year. With partner Almirall, Lilly is exploring dosing once every 12 weeks with data expected in 2027, and it submitted for a pediatric atopic dermatitis indication in the U.S. based on positive phase III results in children 6 months to 18 years old in the ADorable trial program.
quarterly_data.figure: Ebglyss worldwide sales more than doubled year over year; U.S. new-prescription share up approximately 4 percentage points; as few as six maintenance injections per year

quarterly_data.signal: In Oncology, Jaypirca worldwide sales increased 56% compared to Q2 2025 and Lilly received EU approval for Jaypirca in CLL across all lines of therapy. Dan Skovronsky said phase III BRUIN CLL-322, which added pirtobrutinib to a time-limited venetoclax and rituximab regimen in previously treated CLL, reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 45% in the overall study population and by 68% in patients whose disease progressed after one prior covalent BTK inhibitor. He called these the first results to outperform a venetoclax-containing control arm in a CLL phase III trial, with potential to establish a new standard of care, and said the data have been submitted to global regulatory authorities.

quarterly_data.signal: INLURIYO continued strong uptake in the metastatic breast cancer oral SERD market: Lucas Montarce said that after only two full quarters INLURIYO is the U.S. leader in new prescriptions, with more than 50% share. Jake Van Naarden laid out the post-Verzenio breast cancer strategy, saying the three most important targets are the estrogen receptor, CDK4/6 and PI3 kinase alpha, that Lilly believes it has the best medicine for every one of them, and that it plans to combine them. Lilly is on the precipice of beginning the phase III program for tersolisib, its PI3 kinase inhibitor, initially combined with existing endocrine therapies and investigators' choice of CDK4/6 (a large part of which he expects to be Verzenio), and over time envisions combining it with INLURIYO for an all-oral regimen.
quarterly_data.figure: INLURIYO U.S. new-prescription share more than 50% after only two full quarters

quarterly_data.signal: In Neuroscience, Lucas Montarce said KISUNLA posted strong revenue growth and expanded its leadership position in the U.S. anti-amyloid target therapy market, with solid performance in China and Japan contributing to growth as well. He also named KISUNLA alongside MOUNJARO as the driver of Japan's revenue growth in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Retatrutide's efficacy profile is opening indications beyond obesity. Dan Skovronsky said TRIUMPH-1 showed weight loss approaching bariatric surgery levels at the highest doses and clinically meaningful efficacy at low doses with only one titration step, and that in patients with diabetes and obesity retatrutide delivered a magnitude of weight loss not previously seen with incretin therapy. Ken Custer said TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1 showed knee osteoarthritis pain reduced by unprecedented amounts, 75%, that a MASH or MASLD study is ongoing where the glucagon mechanism of action may offer unique opportunities, that a chronic lower back pain study will read out sometime next year, and that Lilly is evaluating several additional indication opportunities internally.
quarterly_data.figure: knee osteoarthritis pain reduced by 75%; weight loss approaching bariatric surgery levels at the highest doses

quarterly_data.signal: Dave Ricks gave the status of the retatrutide filing pathway. Lilly's position is that retatrutide is a biologic application, both in terms of the amino acid count rule and as analogous to a protein. There was a mixed decision in the first court decision and the matter is active litigation; Lilly hopes to come to a conclusion with the FDA to support a BLA application. Lilly has announced it has all the clinical data it needs to submit but still needs to gather a little more on the CMC side, and is in communication with the agency. He added that Lilly has a pretty large lead over any competitors with a triple-acting medicine.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Lilly completed its U.S. submission of orforglipron in Type 2 diabetes, supported by the ACHIEVE phase III program, and presented detailed results from ACHIEVE-2, ACHIEVE-3 and ACHIEVE-5 at the American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions in June. Dan Skovronsky said ACHIEVE-3 was the first head-to-head comparison of two oral GLP-1s and that orforglipron delivered superior glycemic control and weight reduction against 7 mg and 14 mg oral semaglutide in patients with Type 2 diabetes, positioning it as a potential foundational daily oral treatment.
quarterly_data.figure: superior glycemic control and weight reduction versus 7 mg and 14 mg oral semaglutide

quarterly_data.signal: On the shape of the second half, Lucas Montarce said Lilly is upgrading the guide by $2.5 billion for the full-year and walked through the ins and outs. Pre-period adjustments to estimates for rebates and discounts in the U.S., including this quarter, are not expected to continue into the second part of the year. The 2025 base period contains the bolus of MOUNJARO launches in all U.S. markets and new countries in the second half, which will not repeat, so future growth is driven more by penetration in the ex-U.S. market. The guide also factors in the usual Europe Q3 vacation seasonality and U.S. Type 2 diabetes seasonality in the fourth quarter. Measured in dollars rather than percentage growth, he said Lilly expects to continue to drive significant growth in the second part of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: full-year guide upgraded by $2.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Patrik Jonsson gave the ex-U.S. competitive read. MOUNJARO continues to perform very strongly more or less everywhere and has taken a market leadership position across many different markets; in China it obtained category leadership on the NRDL already after 16 months, with significant growth also in Korea, the U.K., Mexico and Germany, and market share in many markets very similar to the level of the U.S. or even above. After generic semaglutide launched in India and Brazil, MOUNJARO total prescriptions continued to grow, and in Canada tirzepatide total prescriptions continue to grow at the same pace as the total market. He said the generic companies have had significant supply constraints, something Lilly needs to monitor very closely, and that tirzepatide's superiority data is a strong first line of defense.
quarterly_data.figure: China NRDL category leadership obtained after 16 months

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa framed the remaining headroom in obesity. Utilization or treatment of obesity is still mid-single-digit in the U.S. and globally, leaving a significant opportunity ahead to capture more patients. He said access is improving meaningfully with Bridge plus some state Medicaid access going live or committing for next year, that overall total prescriptions coming into treatment of obesity are running at 3 million TRxs with growth from both injectable and oral new patients, and that about 55% of overall ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay. Lilly continues to expand its LillyDirect offering, and Patrik Jonsson said versions of LillyDirect have been launched outside the U.S., where the obesity business is still mainly out of pocket and consumer activation is playing a significant role.
quarterly_data.figure: obesity utilization still mid-single-digit; 3 million obesity TRxs; about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions self-pay

quarterly_data.signal: Lilly added new mechanisms and indications outside the incretin franchise. Dan Skovronsky highlighted two recently acquired hematology programs presented at medical meetings, AJ1-11095, a type II JAK inhibitor from Ajax Therapeutics, and KLN-1010, an in vivo CAR T therapy from Kelonia Therapeutics that he later tied to multiple myeloma, both showing compelling early efficacy and safety. Lilly also initiated two phase II trials of brenipatide, its GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, in irritable bowel syndrome, began a phase II trial of its FXR agonist in combination with mirikizumab in Crohn's disease and a phase II trial of its XCL1/2 antibody in vitiligo, and is advancing oral and injectable Lp(a)-lowering drugs in cardiovascular health.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: U.S. FDA approves Inluriyo (imlunestrant) in combination (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA granted full approval to Inluriyo (imlunestrant), an oral estrogen receptor antagonist, in combination with Verzenio (abemaciclib), a CDK4/6 inhibitor, for adults with ER+, HER2-, ESR1-mutated locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (detected by an FDA-authorized test) with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy. The approval rests on the Phase 3 EMBER-3 trial in patients with ESR1-mutated MBC (n=159; Inluriyo n=92, Inluriyo plus Verzenio n=67), where the combination doubled median progression-free survival versus Inluriyo alone, 11.1 months versus 5.5 months (HR=0.53 [95% CI, 0.35–0.80]). Most adverse events with the combination were Grade 1-2; permanent discontinuation of Inluriyo alone due to adverse reactions in the combination arm occurred in 1% of patients and of Verzenio alone in 3.4%. It is Inluriyo's second FDA approval in less than a year, after the September 2025 monotherapy approval, and the combination is now available in the United States. Inluriyo is also in the Phase 3 EMBER-4 adjuvant trial in ER+, HER2- early breast cancer, which Lilly calls the largest adjuvant oral SERD trial, with more than 8,000 patients enrolled across 650+ sites in 30+ countries; initial results are anticipated in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: EMBER-3 ESR1-mutated median PFS 11.1 months versus 5.5 months (HR=0.53); n=159; second FDA approval in less than a year; EMBER-4 more than 8,000 patients, initial results 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: Lilly breaks ground in Houston, one of ten U.S. (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Lilly broke ground on a $6.5 billion active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing site in Houston, Texas, part of the company's $50 billion push to reshore medicine production to meet growing demand at home and export American-made medicines. The site will manufacture Foundayo (orforglipron), Lilly's first synthetic oral GLP-1 medicine, along with other small-molecule medicines and advanced therapeutics including oligonucleotides. Lilly expects it to create more than 600 high-wage jobs plus 4,000 construction jobs while it is built and brought online (no completion date stated), and says the site will use machine learning, AI, digitally integrated systems and advanced data analytics to drive right-first-time execution, with digital automation embedded throughout. Houston is one of ten U.S. manufacturing sites Lilly has announced since 2020: five API sites (Richmond, Virginia; Huntsville, Alabama; Houston, Texas; and two in Lebanon, Indiana - Lebanon API and Lilly Medicine Foundry), four injectable-medicine and device sites (Research Triangle Park and Concord, North Carolina; Kenosha, Wisconsin; Lehigh Valley, Pennsylvania) and one genetic-medicine site (Lebanon Advanced Therapies). Lilly is also providing $12.5 million to a workforce-training relationship with San Jacinto College.
quarterly_data.figure: $6.5 billion Houston API site; part of a $50 billion U.S. reshoring push; more than 600 high-wage jobs and 4,000 construction jobs; ten U.S. sites announced since 2020 (five API)

quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approves Lilly's (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA approved Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa-gobe), a once-weekly basal insulin indicated along with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes; Lilly says it is designed to deliver steady basal insulin levels over a full seven days and to reduce injections by over 300 per year versus once-daily basal insulin. It is Onswik's fourth global approval for adults with type 2 diabetes, following regulatory actions from the EMA, Mexico's COFEPRIS and Japan's PMDA. The approval is based on the QWINT Phase 3 trials in over 3,400 adults with type 2 diabetes; in each QWINT trial once-weekly Onswik met the primary endpoint of non-inferior A1C reduction from baseline comparable to insulin glargine U-100 or insulin degludec U-100, with an overall safety profile similar to the daily basal insulins studied. It should not be used by people with type 1 diabetes due to increased risk of severe hypoglycemia. The Onswik KwikPen will be available in the U.S. in the coming months in two concentrations, 500 units/mL (1,500 units total) and 1,000 units/mL (3,000 units total).
quarterly_data.figure: fourth global approval; QWINT Phase 3 in over 3,400 adults; over 300 fewer injections per year versus once-daily basal insulin; U.S. KwikPen launch in the coming months at 500 units/mL and 1,000 units/mL

quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: La FDA aprueba Mounjaro (tirzepatida) de Lilly para reducir (08-28-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA approved Mounjaro (tirzepatide), the dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke) in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk of these events; it was already approved for glycemic control in adults and children 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes. The approval is based on SURPASS-CVOT (13,299 participants at 640 sites in 30 countries, median follow-up 210.1 weeks), in which Mounjaro was non-inferior to Trulicity (dulaglutide) with an 8% lower rate of MACE-3 (hazard ratio 0.92; 95.3% CI 0.83, 1.01); superiority over dulaglutide was not established, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal. EVP Kenneth Custer called Mounjaro the most-prescribed branded type 2 diabetes medicine for U.S. adults, and Lilly calls it the first and only GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist shown to reduce this risk (company claims). The SURPASS-CVOT data are already in Mounjaro's EU product information and regulatory submissions are under review in additional markets.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. FDA approval of a cardiovascular risk-reduction indication; SURPASS-CVOT MACE-3 8% lower vs Trulicity (HR 0.92), 13,299 participants in 30 countries

quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: FDA approves Lilly's Olumiant (baricitinib) for pediatric (09-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA approved Olumiant (baricitinib), a once-daily oral JAK inhibitor, for pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with severe alopecia areata (AA), expanding its U.S. label beyond adults with rheumatoid arthritis and severe AA. The approval rests on 36-week data from the adolescent cohort of the Phase 3 BRAVE-AA-PEDS study: 80% or more scalp hair coverage (SALT score of 20 or less) in 42% of patients on 4 mg and 27% on 2 mg versus 5% on placebo, and 90% or more coverage (SALT 10 or less) in 37% and 21% versus 2%; the safety profile was consistent with adults, and the U.S. label carries a boxed warning. Olumiant comes as 4 mg, 2 mg and 1 mg tablets (recommended dose 2 mg/day, increased to 4 mg/day if response is inadequate) and is available through specialty pharmacies nationwide; it has coverage at three of the largest pharmacy benefit managers for adults with severe AA. More than 33,000 U.S. patients have been prescribed Olumiant since 2017; it was discovered by Incyte and licensed to Lilly. The European Commission approved Olumiant for adolescents with severe AA in April 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. FDA approval for severe AA in patients 12 and older; BRAVE-AA-PEDS SALT 20 or less in 42% (4 mg) and 27% (2 mg) vs 5% placebo at Week 36; more than 33,000 U.S. patients since 2017; EU adolescent approval April 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-K: capital expenditures were $7.8 billion during 2025, compared to $5.1 billion in 2024. Lilly says it is making investments in global facilities to manufacture existing and future products, which will result in meaningfully higher capital expenditures in the near term; investments to increase manufacturing capacity include new sites in North Carolina, Wisconsin, Indiana, Virginia, Texas, Alabama, Pennsylvania, Ireland, Germany, and the Netherlands.
quarterly_data.figure: capital expenditures $7.8 billion in 2025 vs $5.1 billion in 2024

quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-K: as it expands manufacturing capacity, Lilly has entered, and expects to continue to enter, into agreements for contract manufacturing and for supply of materials; executed agreements related to its medicines in development could, under certain circumstances, require it to pay up to approximately $10 billion if it does not purchase specified amounts of goods or services over the durations of the agreements, which are generally up to 8 years. Lilly also says it has expanded relationships with contract manufacturing organizations, artificial intelligence vendors and other third parties in recent periods.
quarterly_data.figure: up to approximately $10 billion in minimum-purchase supply commitments; agreement durations generally up to 8 years

quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-Q: purchases of property and equipment were $5,259 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026 vs $3,207 million a year earlier, and expenditures for long-lived assets were $2,906 million in Q2 2026 vs $1,985 million in Q2 2025; Lilly says its investments in global facilities to manufacture existing and future products will result in meaningfully higher capital expenditures in the near term.
quarterly_data.figure: 1H 2026 purchases of property and equipment $5,259 million (vs $3,207 million); Q2 2026 expenditures for long-lived assets $2,906 million (vs $1,985 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: Lilly's Jaypirca (pirtobrutinib), the first-and-only (10-02-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA approved an additional indication for Jaypirca (pirtobrutinib, 100 mg and 50 mg tablets), a non-covalent BTK inhibitor, for adults with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) with no known 17p deletion, allowing first-line use for appropriate patients. The approval rests on the Phase 3 BRUIN CLL-313 trial versus bendamustine plus rituximab (n=141 per arm): at a median follow-up of 28 months, IRC-assessed progression-free survival improved with HR=0.20 (median not yet reached versus 33.5 months), and overall response rate was 94% versus 81%. Lilly calls Jaypirca the first-and-only FDA-approved non-covalent BTK inhibitor (company claim). Jacob Van Naarden, president of Lilly Oncology: the approval expands 'its potential to reach more patients who may benefit - this time as an initial treatment.'
quarterly_data.figure: BRUIN CLL-313 PFS HR=0.20; median PFS not reached vs 33.5 months; ORR 94% vs 81%; n=141 per arm

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa (EVP, President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities) on U.S. obesity access: commercial coverage has been relatively stagnant on 50%; some employers recently removed coverage while Lilly is in discussions with many employers on adding it, and he does not see a step change coming into 2027 in either direction. He called Bridge in Medicare probably the single largest driver of increased access, with some states starting to add Medicaid coverage. Lilly's Employer Connect program has a network of more than 20 third-party providers actively talking to employers, and he believes a number of employers will opt in or maintain coverage through it for 2027 (benefit decisions are typically announced before October).
quarterly_data.figure: commercial coverage relatively stagnant on 50%; more than 20 third-party providers in the Employer Connect network

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa on Lilly's just-published Zepbound cost-of-care study of direct medical costs in people 55 and over: savings start as early as 6 months, and at 12 months reach upwards of $600 per month per person of benefit, which he said more than offsets the cost of the medicine. He expects the accumulating evidence to convince more employers and payers, while saying it will take time and more than one study to change their calculus.
quarterly_data.figure: savings from 6 months; upwards of $600 per month per person at 12 months (people 55 and over)

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa on the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge rollout: around 20 million eligible on Lilly's estimate of the criteria, and around 600,000 people using it so far (he also cited Dr. Oz's figure of close to 600,000). Bridge applies one standard set of criteria across Medicare eligibility; there were some minor hiccups in the first days but overall it is working really well. Uptake shows a preference toward injectables and toward Zepbound (the KwikPen, available through Bridge and for self-pay), with good uptake of Foundayo within Bridge as well. He expects the uptake and the savings evidence to be a net positive toward finding a solution past 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: around 600,000 people using Bridge; around 20 million eligible

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa on U.S. launch metrics (the transcript names the brand Zepbound throughout this passage): Lilly now has more than 30% share in new starts within oral GLP-1, which he called a marked improvement in just the last two months of new starts, with progress in the covered commercial segment, Bridge and self-pay. Most starts are currently self-pay at lower initial price points until people get through to higher doses, a mix he said will shift over time. He said Lilly will continue to challenge its teams to get leading share with Foundayo, but would not commit to a time for getting there.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 30% share in new starts within oral GLP-1

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa on the ex-U.S. Foundayo rollout: Foundayo is now launched in the UAE and the U.K., where early indications are positive and expansive - new patients are being treated, the total market and Lilly's overall share are both growing, and it is not cannibalizing Mounjaro. Lilly plans to launch in Saudi Arabia and Mexico after the recent approvals; it is submitted in over 40 markets and will launch as approvals come, with supply readily available and commercial teams ready. Around 75% of the market outside the U.S. is self-pay.
quarterly_data.figure: launched in the UAE and the U.K.; submitted in over 40 markets; around 75% of the ex-U.S. market self-pay

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa on adherence: it is early days, but Foundayo second-fill data are very good, consistent with other oral medications and not that far off injectables. For context, Trulicity has been the adherence gold standard, approaching a 16-month average, and Lilly sees Mounjaro and Zepbound in that same realm, while most chronic therapies have persistence of less than 8 months. He anticipates Foundayo adherence probably better than typical chronic disease; whether it matches injectables, 'we'll see'.
quarterly_data.figure: Trulicity approaching a 16-month average adherence; most chronic therapies less than 8 months persistence

quarterly_data.signal: Ilya Yuffa on eloralintide phase II results: even at the lower starting doses it showed placebo-like tolerability with 13% efficacy, and up to 20% efficacy in monotherapy. Lilly is also studying it with tirzepatide to see whether an add-on can amplify efficacy without compromising tolerability, and he sees it as both a monotherapy and a future add-on in the obesity portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: 13% efficacy at lower starting doses; up to 20% efficacy in monotherapy (phase II)

players.product: AI-designed small-molecule programs

quarterly_data.signal: Head of research Mike Quigley said two external opportunities entered phase I in the second quarter, with internal projects to follow, and that 'This year alone, we plan approximately one new phase I start every two months, a meaningful step up as the changes in research take flight.' He also published an updated epidemiology data book providing the latest estimates across many indications represented in Sanofi's portfolio and pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: ~1 new phase I start every two months; 2 external opportunities entered phase I in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: New CEO Belén Garijo made R&D productivity the central theme, saying the pipeline needs 'greater scientific rigor, fact-based decision making, a stronger, even if linear, governance, and more effective operations,' and launched a comprehensive outside-in portfolio review focused on the later-stage pipeline. Several phase III programs failed or were stopped in the quarter: two Dupixent studies in lichen simplex chronicus, the second venglustat study in Fabry disease and riliprubart in refractory CIDP stopped early on an IDMC recommendation. Itepekimab programs across COPD and chronic rhinosinusitis and balinatunfib programs were discontinued, and amlitelimab will not progress to regulatory submission.

quarterly_data.signal: Asked how much of the EUR 10 billion R&D budget is discovery versus development, Belén Garijo said 'The majority of the R&D budget is clinical development,' and Mike Quigley added 'there's not a linear relationship between spend and outcome,' emphasizing dynamic capital allocation away from unpromising medicines. Management expects moderate increases in R&D spend in the short term, growing at a lower level than sales. François Roger said Sanofi invested EUR 47 billion in BD and M&A over the last eight years and lost EUR 7 billion of it, and that BD and M&A activity will intensify to address pipeline weakness.

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter net sales grew 17.8% to EUR 11.6 billion, primarily volume-driven, with growth of around 15% restating for Dynavax and Blueprint. Dupixent grew 37% and exceeded EUR 5 billion of quarterly sales for the first time with more than 1.5 million patients under treatment; launch medicines grew over 60% and now represent 13% of sales; rare disease sales reached nearly EUR 1.9 billion, up 24%; vaccines declined 5% to EUR 1.15 billion, with Beyfortus up 54% to EUR 108 million and HEPLISAV-B up 43% pro forma to EUR 113 million. Business operating income rose 35.8% and business EPS grew 33.3%, or 21% underlying.

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance was upgraded to sales growth of around 10% at constant exchange rates with business EPS growing slightly faster than sales; the full-year tax rate is now expected at around 21%. The combined 2030 ambition was raised by almost 10% on a like-for-like basis at constant exchange rates: Dupixent to about EUR 25 billion, pharmaceutical launches to about EUR 10 billion and vaccines to about EUR 9 billion, the vaccines cut split equally between currency and U.S. vaccination coverage rate dynamics.

quarterly_data.signal: Upcoming catalysts: the final phase III readout for Sarclisa in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma is expected in the remainder of 2026 and efdoralprin alfa phase II AATD emphysema data will support FDA discussions on a potential submission already in the second half. In 2027 Sanofi expects phase II-B results for brivekimig in hidradenitis suppurativa, frexalimab in relapsing multiple sclerosis, riliprubart versus IVIG in CIDP in the latter half of 2027, and pneumococcal and yellow fever vaccine readouts; frexalimab in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis reads out in 2028. Venglustat has U.S. priority review in type 3 Gaucher disease with a target action date of November 25th.

ALTUVIIIO continued its momentum in hemophilia A and 'remains the top choice for patient switches in the U.S.'; AYVAKIT keeps expanding in systemic mastocytosis, driven by continued growth in the number of patients treated and duration of treatment; Sarclisa is performing well in multiple myeloma following the subcutaneous regulatory approval; HEPLISAV-B made a significant contribution; and the recently launched rare disease medicines Wayrilz and Qfitlia are starting to show momentum. Management expects the portfolio to keep driving meaningful growth as these medicines and vaccines launch in new geographies.

Like-for-like H1 growth, restating for products such as AYVAKIT last year, was about 27%, against the 15% average CAGR needed to reach EUR 10 billion by 2030 - 'Given that we are on a trend of 27% today, I'm not worried at all about our capacity to reach the EUR 10 billion.' All of these products are already in the market, so it is 'essentially commercial risk', and the portfolio is already positive in terms of BOI despite Sanofi still being in an investment position behind it.

quarterly_data.signal: Management detailed the Dupixent quarter. CFO Francois Roger said growth nine years after launch is 'essentially volume-led' and included 'a couple of hundred millions of positive adjustments in growth to net' that will not repeat later in the year; Sanofi does not disclose the volume versus price breakdown. Head of Specialty Care Manuela Buxo said the non-recurring gross-to-net portion is 'a couple of hundred million', while the recurring portion is largely enhanced 340B control, part of which continues in the second half, and that IQVIA TRX script data does not fully reflect total demand, which is higher. In the U.S. Dupixent remains the number 1 prescribed biologic across important prescriber groups; growth moderates in H2 on a higher comparison base and as indication launches annualize.

CEO Belen Garijo added that Sanofi plans on 'a base case that is associated to the loss of the product patent'.
quarterly_data.figure: Dupixent patent expiration date up to 2046; protected beyond March 2031; nine indications to date

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Francois Roger said gross margin increased by 3.7 percentage points, benefiting from the reversal of inventory provisions following the Sarclisa subcutaneous regulatory approval. Excluding that item the underlying gross margin increase was around 1.7 percentage points, driven by favorable product mix and efficiency.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin +3.7 percentage points reported, around +1.7 percentage points underlying

CEO Belen Garijo noted established medicines were stable in the quarter, and CFO Francois Roger explained the reallocation behind that: commercial spend that used to sit behind now-mature General Medicines products has been moved 'behind growth assets, essentially within Specialty Care and starting with Dupixent'. He added 'We don't manage fixed budget within a certain category of investments' and said there is no rule that resources freed by terminated programs must be reallocated to R&D - allocation follows contribution to growth and return, including on the commercial and industrial side.

quarterly_data.signal: Business operating income margin expanded by 3.8 percentage points, driven by gross leverage, cost discipline and some favorable phasing of capital gains that were roughly EUR 80 million higher this quarter compared to last year. CFO Francois Roger put underlying BOI growth at around 20%.
quarterly_data.figure: BOI margin +3.8 percentage points; capital gains roughly EUR 80 million higher YoY; underlying BOI growth around 20%

quarterly_data.signal: For the first half CFO Francois Roger reported sales growth of 15.7% and business EPS growth of 22.7%, with underlying sales growth around 13% - reported sales partly driven by acquisitions and reported EPS by positive one-offs. He guided to tougher comps and 'some deceleration of our sales growth' in H2, lapping last year's strong momentum from Dupixent's new indication and the consolidation of AYVAKIT that began in July 2025, plus fewer one-off benefits to gross margin, no further Regeneron development balance reimbursement and reduced benefits from share buyback.

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Francois Roger said Q2 marks the end of the Regeneron development balance reimbursement. For full year 2026 the increase in Amvuttra royalties fully offsets that negative BOI impact, but in 2027 there will be a negative EUR 200 million BOI gap between the two items: a final negative BOI impact from the Regeneron reimbursement of about EUR 600 million year on year from 2026 to 2027, against Amvuttra royalty income expected to increase by about EUR 400 million year on year. Sanofi also introduced Amvuttra royalty projections until 2030 based on VARA consensus, and said recent competitor data supports its confidence in the medicine's long-term potential.

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Francois Roger expects vaccine sales growth to be slightly negative in 2026, mainly crystallizing in H2 on the usual seasonality, and for Q3 specifically 'a low- to mid-teens sales decrease, reflecting a different distribution between Q3 and Q4 of our respiratory vaccine sales compared to last year'. The Q2 influenza decline came from the 2025 one-offs and a lower southern hemisphere season, while birth cohort dynamics weighed on the pediatric franchise. Head of Vaccines Thomas Triomphe said one half of the 2030 vaccine ambition reduction is pure U.S. dollar to euro exchange rate and the second half is U.S. vaccination coverage rate evolution 'weaker than expected following the new U.S. administration', mostly in the respiratory area - classical flu and RSV - with CDC data also showing a decrease in the vaccination coverage rate of U.S. pediatric vaccines. He said the long-term ambition is unchanged, with fundamentals supported by a growing elderly population and a pipeline focused on the elderly segment.

quarterly_data.signal: Head of research Mike Quigley listed the quarter's regulatory approvals: a U.S. label expansion for Dupixent in chronic spontaneous urticaria in children, a U.S. label expansion for TZIELD in Stage 3 Type 1 diabetes, Wayrilz in Japan for immune thrombocytopenia, EU approval for Cenrifki in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis in patients without relapses, and Sarclisa becoming the first anticancer medicine approved in the U.S., EU and Japan to be given either subcutaneously or via an on-body injector, plus four regulatory designations. The Sarclisa CirCLIQ on-body injector is 'a compact, battery-free device with a hidden needle that automatically delivers the medicine with no manual push and no bioactive excipients', designed to enable potential at-home administration by a healthcare professional or the patient and potentially supported by telemedicine; a regulatory decision in China is expected next year.

quarterly_data.signal: At ATS Sanofi presented phase II data for efdoralprin alfa in AATD emphysema showing superiority over standard of care in achieving and maintaining normalized functional AAT levels: dosed every three weeks it achieved mean functional AAT trough levels more than three times higher than those observed with weekly plasma-derived AAT at week 32 and was detected in every lung lobe of each participant at week 24, with a safety profile comparable to the current standard of care. Phase III results for Nexviazyme in infantile-onset Pompe disease showed 94% of infants alive and free from invasive ventilation at week 52, with improvements across all key secondary endpoints; head of research Mike Quigley said the data support FDA discussions on a U.S. label expansion, as approvals were already secured elsewhere.

CEO Belen Garijo confirmed that 'together with our partners, we have already defined the next two indications', making duvakitug one of the few immunology programs being expanded rather than cut this quarter.

On frexalimab, Sanofi has been actively working with global regulators to refine its statistical analysis plan given the recent performance of comparators in RMS studies; the primary endpoint does not change in the context of annual relapse rates, with added focus on key secondary endpoints including a six-month disability progression. On riliprubart, the IDMC recommended not moving forward with MOBILIZE because the study was unlikely to meet its primary endpoint, but Quigley stressed the two patient populations are very different - MOBILIZE enrolled refractory, hard-to-treat patients with nothing available to them, while VITALIZE enrolls patients on IVIG who are still progressing - and the same IDMC reviewed VITALIZE and recommended progressing it forward.

CFO Francois Roger, who has taken business development under his remit, said the strategy must evolve from essentially early-stage assets toward 'more interest for late-stage assets and potentially commercial assets', that it need not be one single deal, and that 'there is no dramatic urgency in terms of BD M&A. We are not driven by any timing objective.' He said substantial value has been created historically from the remaining EUR 40 billion of past BD and M&A investment, and that BD will only work if it stays in very close proximity to the R&D organization.

The scope will broaden beyond rare genetic disorders to leverage those capabilities, and Sanofi has tailored the portfolio for China, recently launching two innovative medicines there: Myqorzo, a cardiac myosin inhibitor for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and rovadicitinib, the first ROCK/JAK dual-acting inhibitor for myelofibrosis.

Head of Vaccines Thomas Triomphe has been nominated to lead China and starts September 1st; he said Sanofi wants to accelerate its efforts in the Chinese innovation ecosystem and also learn from the competitiveness of the local pharmaceutical marketplace, in extremely close collaboration with R&D.

quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: Positive interim data shows Roche's sefaxersen (09-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Roche announced positive prespecified interim results from the ongoing phase III IMAgINATION study of investigational sefaxersen (a once-monthly subcutaneous antisense oligonucleotide inhibiting complement factor B, designed for self-administration) in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) at high risk of progression. The study met its primary endpoint: statistically significant and clinically meaningful proteinuria reduction versus placebo at 37 weeks, measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR); no absolute effect size was disclosed. Safety and tolerability were consistent with previously reported data, with no new safety signals. IMAgINATION enrolled 459 people randomised 1:1 to sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks and continues blinded to evaluate eGFR at week 105. Interim data will be presented at an upcoming medical congress and shared with health authorities (no filing date stated). Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis. The company says sefaxersen is the first mRNA-targeted therapy for IgAN and shows best-in-class potential (company claims).
quarterly_data.figure: phase III IMAgINATION met primary endpoint (UPCR at 37 weeks); 459 patients, 105-week study

quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: [Ad hoc announcement pursuant to Art. 53 LR] Roche (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Ad hoc announcement: positive topline results from the Phase II CT-388-104 trial of enicepatide (CT-388), an investigational once-weekly subcutaneous dually biased GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, in 447 adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity; both primary endpoints (HbA1c and body weight at 48 weeks) were met. At the highest 24 mg dose: mean HbA1c reduction of 2.65% from a baseline of 8.1%; 4.13% HbA1c reduction in patients with baseline HbA1c >8.5%; 90% reached HbA1c ≤6.5% and 62% reached normoglycemia (HbA1c < 5.7%); mean weight loss of 15.5% at 48 weeks without a demonstrable plateau. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 2.0% in enicepatide arms vs 0.0% for placebo, with mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal effects. Roche has two ongoing Phase III studies in chronic weight management (ENITH-1 and ENITH-2) and plans to initiate a Phase III glycemic-control program and cardiovascular outcomes trials in the first half of 2027. The company describes a potential best-in-disease profile (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: 24 mg: HbA1c -2.65% (baseline 8.1%), -4.13% if baseline >8.5%; 90% at ≤6.5%, 62% < 5.7%; weight loss 15.5% at 48 weeks; 447 patients; Phase III glycemic and CVOT start first half of 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: European Commission approves Roche's Susvimo for the (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The European Commission approved Susvimo (ranibizumab 100 mg/mL) for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), delivered continuously into the eye via the Contivue refillable implant (Port Delivery Platform, CE-marked in the EU in 2025), with as few as two treatments per year. Approval rests on the Phase III Archway study (vision equivalent to monthly intravitreal ranibizumab injections) plus the Phase II Ladder study and the Portal extension study (vision maintained for up to seven years); with two refills per year approximately 95% of patients needed no supplemental anti-VEGF treatment. nAMD affects approximately 1.7 million people across the EU. Roche is evaluating other pipeline molecules for use with the Port Delivery Platform. The company says Susvimo is the first and only continuous delivery treatment offering an alternative to standard-of-care eye injections for nAMD (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: EC approval; ~95% needed no supplemental anti-VEGF with two refills per year; ~1.7 million nAMD patients in the EU

quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: CHMP recommends EU approval of Roche's Ocrevus for children (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP recommended approval of Ocrevus (ocrelizumab) IV infusion for paediatric patients aged 10 years and older with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis; a final European Commission decision is expected in the near future. The U.S. FDA approved Ocrevus for paediatric RMS patients in May 2026. Basis is the Phase III OPERETTA 2 study: non-inferior to fingolimod on relapse control (48% relapse-risk reduction vs fingolimod) and superior on brain lesions (new or enlarging T2 lesions -48%, gadolinium-enhancing active T1 lesions -87%), with safety aligned to the established profile across more than 525,000 adult patients globally. The company cites at least 40,000 children and adolescents living with MS worldwide, roughly one-third in Europe.
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion (ages 10+); relapse risk -48% vs fingolimod; T2 lesions -48%, T1 lesions -87%; FDA paediatric approval May 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Vertex press release: Vertex Announces Positive Results From Phase 2b AMPLIFIED (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Vertex reported positive results from the Phase 2b AMPLIFIED study of inaxaplin (45 mg once daily on top of optimized standard of care) in APOL1-mediated kidney disease (AMKD); forty-one people were enrolled and dosed in two cohorts. In cohort 1, AMKD with modest proteinuria (N=23), UACR fell -42.7% (95% CI -58.3%, -21.1%) at Week 13 versus baseline and UPCR fell -44.7%, in line with the Phase 2a FSGS study (-43.4% UACR, -47.6% UPCR); most cohort 1 patients were not diagnosed with FSGS. In cohort 2, AMKD with type 2 diabetes (N=18), UACR fell -17.3% (95% CI -36.3%, 7.2%) and UPCR -25.4%. Inaxaplin was generally safe and well tolerated: no serious adverse events related to inaxaplin, all adverse events mild or moderate, most common headache (7.3%), and five people had isolated, asymptomatic transaminase elevations that resolved. CMO Carmen Bozic said Vertex looks forward to discussing the AMPLIFIED results with regulators in the context of the AMPLITUDE pivotal study.
quarterly_data.figure: cohort 1 UACR -42.7% and UPCR -44.7% at Week 13; cohort 2 (type 2 diabetes) UACR -17.3% and UPCR -25.4%; forty-one people dosed at 45 mg once daily; headache 7.3%
