Vertex says the deal establishes rare endocrine diseases as its next pillar of growth, that PALSONIFY and atumelnant have the potential to deliver more than $5 billion in combined annual revenue at peak, and that it is expected to become accretive to non-GAAP operating income in 2029. CEO Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex looks forward to continuing to launch PALSONIFY globally and accelerating the atumelnant program.

quarterly_data.quarter: Jazz Pharmaceuticals press release: U.S. FDA Approves Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) with and (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA approved two Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA): Ziihera plus Tevimbra (tislelizumab-jsgr) and fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy for HER2+ IHC 3+ and IHC 2+/ISH+ disease regardless of PD-L1 status, and Ziihera plus the same chemotherapy for HER2+ IHC 3+ disease. In the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial both Ziihera combinations reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 35% and extended median PFS to 12.4 months versus 8.1 months with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy; the tislelizumab triplet reduced the risk of death by 28%, with median OS of 26.4 months versus 19.2 months. The U.S. label carries boxed warnings for diarrhea and embryo-fetal toxicity. CMO Rob Iannone called Ziihera the first and only bispecific HER2-targeted antibody combined with a PD-1 inhibitor and chemotherapy approved for all HER2+ advanced GEA patients regardless of PD-L1 status (company claim). Approximately 20% of GEA patients have HER2+ disease.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. FDA approval of two first-line HER2+ GEA regimens; HERIZON-GEA-01 PFS risk reduced 35%, median PFS 12.4 vs 8.1 months; triplet death risk reduced 28%, median OS 26.4 vs 19.2 months

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce on XYWAV durability: 'We have not really seen any material impacts from those generics coming into the market,' and '80% or more patients with narcolepsy and IH have comorbidities, cardiovascular and cardiometabolic comorbidities,' which keeps the low-sodium option important. Orexins will enter in the NT1 indication, 'which is less than half of the overall narcolepsy space'; from what Jazz understands, healthcare providers will not switch the stable base of XYWAV patients away, though 'it takes longer for patients to get to Xywav if they are trying the orexin first,' and 'we do not see this business being dramatically disrupted.' On idiopathic hypersomnia she cited estimates of a prevalent population 'maybe similar to narcolepsy, maybe 100,000 patients', diagnosed patients 'around about 37,000' and treated patients 'maybe 9,000', leaving significant room for XYWAV to grow.

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce: Epidiolex delivered '$292 million, 16% revenue growth, 14% volume growth' in the second quarter. Much of the growth comes from the adult segment, which is more fragmented than the pediatric segment and still has significant headroom, and Jazz is investing in JazzCares support to keep patients on treatment longer. Because Epidiolex is weight-based, adults can take a large volume of the sesame-oil-based oral solution, which can limit adult uptake; Jazz expects the capsule formulation (NDA submitted) to expand the overall patient pool. She said the ANDA settlements out to the late 2030s opened the opportunity to invest in a phase III DEE study, a phase II/III study in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, an adult LGS study and an earlier focal-onset seizure study.

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce on Zepzelca: since the first-line maintenance launch Jazz's focus has been '100% commercially on first-line', which generated around 30%-40% of second-quarter revenue; the second-line business is expected to taper away, and she expects the first-line segment to 'become a little bit more competitive with the entrance of new competitors', while Zepzelca is particularly appreciated in the community setting because it is easier to use without the monitoring.
quarterly_data.figure: around 30%-40% of Q2 Zepzelca revenue from first-line maintenance

quarterly_data.signal: Head of IR John Bluth on business development: the focus is rare disease where Jazz has competency in epilepsy, sleep and oncology, citing over the past 12 to 18 months the Chimerix acquisition (Modeyso), the Saniona acquisition of early epilepsy opportunities, the AbCellera deal in oncology and, most recently, Actio Biosciences in epilepsy. Outside its core areas Jazz is 'less likely to go very early' and more likely to look at proof of concept or later; inside them it is open to earlier transactions and closer-to-commercial deals - 'Look for more from us going forward.' CCO Sam Pearce expects 'very significant commercial synergies' from Actio's KCNT1 epilepsy asset, which shares the core call point with pediatric epileptologists that Epidiolex has; she said additional commercial investments have not yet been detailed. Bluth added that as the Actio transaction closes, the Jazz team will step in and drive the program forward.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on the first-line GEA launch of Ziihera: Jazz will report Ziihera revenues quarterly as the best measure of the launch, and with BTC already at more than 50% share, growth from here will be driven by GEA uptake. Launch communication will focus on the triplet regimen, which she called the most appropriate choice given more than 2 years overall survival benefit and use for both PD-L1 positive and PD-L1 negative patients ('probably the first time' - company claim), with the doublet available for patients for whom an immunotherapy is not appropriate. Drawing on GPO contracting experience in the community setting, she does not anticipate significant adoption differences between Medicare and commercial patients. GEA represents 'a sizable proportion' of the $3 billion-$5 billion peak, breast cancer is one of the largest tumor types longer term, and she said Ziihera 'can represent a new standard of care for all HER2 expressing cancers.'
quarterly_data.figure: GEA a sizable proportion of the $3 billion-$5 billion Ziihera peak; BTC share more than 50%

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on Epidiolex: the remaining in-label opportunity is particularly the adult long-term care segment, where many LGS patients do not yet have a definitive diagnosis, so Jazz has invested in tools that help physicians diagnose LGS; enrollment in JazzCares extends persistency. She expects the capsule formulation to bring both some conversion of oral-solution patients and incremental growth in the adult segment, without being specific, and said access 'has always been very strong for Epidiolex.' Of the four Epidiolex studies she sized two new populations: 'about 120,000 to 150,000 U.S. patients' in the phase III DEE segment and JME 'around about 60,000 U.S. patients'; the JME study uses the capsule formulation.
quarterly_data.figure: DEE about 120,000 to 150,000 U.S. patients; JME around about 60,000 U.S. patients

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on XYWAV: roughly two-thirds of net patient adds over the last few quarters have come from idiopathic hypersomnia, where XYWAV 'remains the only licensed product', and the undiagnosed prevalent population could be significantly larger than the diagnosed base. On orexins, Jazz does not yet know how they will be priced or whether payers will support combination therapy; it does not anticipate the stable XYWAV base being switched to an orexin, but 'we may, in time, see some impact there on the pace with which we add patients onto the Xywav.'
quarterly_data.figure: roughly two-thirds of XYWAV net patient adds from IH

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on the Actio ABS-1230 KCNT1 epilepsy asset (she said the deal still needs to close): around 2,500 U.S. patients are diagnosed with KCNT1 epilepsy and, she thinks, prevalence is similar outside the U.S., making it 'an exciting global opportunity for Jazz'; testing is already reflexive for children with epilepsy, and patients can have potentially 100 or so seizures a day. Jazz executive John said Jazz is 'seeing a lot of substrate, especially in epilepsy and oncology', has the balance-sheet capacity for more deals, sets no limits on geography in sourcing, and would fully maximize any asset with broader-than-rare potential, as with Ziihera.
quarterly_data.figure: around 2,500 U.S. KCNT1 epilepsy patients; prevalence outside the U.S. similar (CCO: 'I think')

quarterly_data.signal: Jazz executive John: Jazz is 'leaning very heavily' into AI to increase efficiency, with company-wide AI utilization goals and specific use cases in finance, commercial and clinical functions. CCO Samantha Pearce said Jazz set up a new customer-experience part of its commercial organization that uses data, AI and predictive algorithms to identify patients and those at risk of dropping off treatment - for XYWAV, predicting when patients may fall off therapy so patient support programs can intervene, and for Ziihera, understanding when and where GEA patients are diagnosed in a fragmented community setting and feeding next best actions to the sales teams.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

players.product: precision-oncology companion diagnostic programs

quarterly_data.signal: The phase III CLARITY-Gastric01 trial of sonesitatug vedotin demonstrated an overall survival benefit in patients with CLDN18.2 expression as low as 25% at any staining intensity, a lower threshold than that required by other CLDN18.2 targeted therapies. Dave Fredrickson said the company expanded the definition of CLDN18.2 positivity with a cutoff of greater than 25%, which represents about half of patients with gastric GEJ cancer, or more than 180,000 patients across the U.S., EU5, China and Japan. Management estimated peak year revenue of $3 billion-$5 billion for the ADC.
quarterly_data.figure: CLDN18.2 cutoff >25%; ~50% of 2L+ gastric patients; >180,000 patients; peak revenue $3B-$5B

quarterly_data.signal: Biomarker testing infrastructure was flagged as a commercial gating factor. For Truqap in PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer following the CAPItello-281 approval, management said 'a near-term priority is to establish testing in the setting, which today is not common practice.' Truqap revenue was $233 million in the quarter, up 37%. In the AVANZAR trial both the intention-to-treat and the TROP2 biomarker-positive populations sit at the top of the multiple testing procedure, so a positive study can come from either group. For Ultomiris in HSCT-TMA, discussions with health authorities are ongoing on interpreting the data 'including in the context of real-world evidence.'
quarterly_data.figure: Truqap revenue $233M (+37%)

quarterly_data.signal: Core R&D expense increased 6% in the first half and represented 23% of total revenue; management expects full-year R&D at the upper end of the low 20s percentage range as it builds out bispecifics, cell therapies and T-cell engagers. Capital expenditure was $1.5 billion in the first half and is expected to increase by around a third in 2026, including a new ADC manufacturing facility in Singapore, and the company opened a new Kendall Square R&D center in Cambridge. Deal-related payments totaled $3.3 billion and new BD transactions totaled just over $2 billion in upfront payments year to date.
quarterly_data.figure: core R&D +6%, 23% of revenue; H1 capex $1.5B, +~1/3 in 2026; deal payments $3.3B; BD upfronts >$2B YTD

quarterly_data.signal: Six high-value phase III programs read out positively in the first half, including first pivotal data for three new molecular entities, and the company secured 30 major market approvals. Pascal Soriot said 25 key phase III trial readouts are planned over the next 18 months, with pivotal data readouts for six new molecular entities in 2027 alone. Saruparib in prostate cancer was singled out as a $5 billion-range opportunity reading out next year.
quarterly_data.figure: 25 phase III readouts in 18 months; 6 NME pivotal readouts in 2027; 30 major market approvals in H1

quarterly_data.signal: First-half total revenue grew 6%, or 11% excluding Farxiga and Brilinta which are affected by generics, and core EPS grew 11%. Oncology total revenue grew 15% to $14.1 billion with the U.S. up 18% and Europe up 16%; Rare Disease grew 11% to $4.9 billion; BioPharmaceuticals declined 5% to $11.2 billion on loss of exclusivity for Farxiga, Brilinta and roxadustat. Core gross margin was 83% in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: total revenue +6% (+11% ex-Farxiga/Brilinta); core EPS +11%; oncology $14.1B (+15%); rare disease $4.9B (+11%); BioPharma $11.2B (-5%); core gross margin 83%

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year guidance was reiterated: total revenue to increase by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core EPS by a low double-digit percentage at constant exchange rates. Management reaffirmed the risk-adjusted $80 billion revenue ambition for 2030, noting 11 approved new molecular entities against a target of 20 by 2030, and said it does not need additional business development to deliver post-2030 growth.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue mid-to-high single digit; core EPS low double digit CER; $80B by 2030; 11 of 20 NMEs approved

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter regulatory output: Pascal Soriot said the company 'received eight major market approvals across important indications, including two additional NMEs.' These included the first approvals for Enhertu in first-line hormone receptor-positive breast cancer with emergent ESR1 mutations in Europe and Japan and a few other countries, with constructive discussions continuing with the U.S. FDA, and U.S. FDA approval for Baxfendy, 'which has the potential to transform outcomes for patients with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension.' For the first half he identified the two first NME approvals as camizestrant in breast cancer and Baxfendy in hypertension.
quarterly_data.figure: 8 major market approvals in Q2 including two additional NMEs

quarterly_data.signal: China: Pascal Soriot said growth 'was impacted by continued effects from volume-based procurement, and we expect the recent NRDL additions and new regulatory approval in 2026 to fuel future growth,' while the U.S., Europe and emerging markets outside of China grew strongly. Asked whether he was still confident on the country, he said he remains 'still very bullish for reasons that have evolved' - Chinese companies are innovating at great speed and tend to partner with global companies to globalize development and commercialization, competition in the Tagrisso market and the ADC market is very intense, and being strongly present in China let the Chinese team play a role in the speedy development of Sone-Ve.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Core P&L detail below the top line. CFO Aradhana Sarin said product revenue grew 6% in the first half while alliance revenue increased by 29%, 'reflecting higher profit shares from our partnered medicines Enhertu, Datverzo, and Tezspire in markets where our partners record product sales.' Core gross margin of 83% improved in the second quarter compared to the first, but a lower second-half margin is expected 'consistent with prior years, reflecting seasonal demand patterns for lower-margin medicines such as FluMist and Beyfortus,' with full-year core gross margin stable to slightly higher versus 2025. Core SG&A expense also increased by 6% in the first half, covering the U.S. Baxfendy launch and pre-launch investment ahead of tozorakimab. Other operating income was $341 million in the first six months, consisting of royalties and small regional divestitures, with a broadly similar level anticipated in the second half; in Q&A she added there is a portion of it 'that is consistent and will likely continue into 2027.' Guidance for 2027 will be given at the beginning of 2027, after an annual budgeting process that starts later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: product revenue +6%; alliance revenue +29%; core gross margin 83% in H1; core SG&A +6%; other operating income $341M

quarterly_data.signal: Cash, working capital and capital structure. Aradhana Sarin reported '$1.2 billion in the first half, a decline versus comparator period' (the transcript drops the line-item label), which 'primarily reflects the Lynparza milestone received in the first quarter of 2025, skewing comparisons, as well as working capital impact associated with U.S. loss of exclusivity for Farxiga'; those working capital effects are expected to persist through the remainder of the year before normalizing. The second-quarter tax rate benefited from a one-time adjustment to deferred tax assets following certain internal legal entity changes. Deal-related payments included the $1.2 billion upfront payment for the CSPC collaboration, which closed during the second quarter, and the company continues to expect milestone payments of approximately $2.5 billion for the full year relating to prior business development transactions, with the most recently announced Dizal transaction included in the year-to-date BD upfronts. Net debt increased by around $3.5 billion in the first half, primarily reflecting the second FY 2025 interim dividend paid in March and those deal payments; the company remains comfortable with its level of gross debt, and core finance costs are expected to be higher in the second half following refinancing at higher than historic interest rates and lower interest income.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.2B in H1 (decline vs comparator period); CSPC upfront $1.2B; FY milestone payments ~$2.5B; net debt +~$3.5B

quarterly_data.signal: EGFR-mutated lung franchise. Dave Fredrickson said Tagrisso delivered 6% growth in the second quarter to revenues of $1.9 billion, supported by double-digit growth in the U.S., and that it is the number one prescribed third-generation EGFR TKI globally, approved across all stages of disease; in the highly competitive U.S. market FLAURA2 holds around three-quarters of the growing first-line combination segment. Against the MARIPOSA regimen and intense Chinese competition he said 'we're seeing double-digit volume growth, and in fact, double-digit revenue growth in the U.S.' AstraZeneca also announced the in-licensing of Zegfrovy, a novel oral EGFR inhibitor already approved in the U.S. and China for tumors carrying exon 20 insertion mutations following progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy; based on the WU-KONG28 data presented at ASCO, first-line filings have been submitted in China and the U.S. Susan Galbraith said the asset, licensed from Dizal, is also active in non-classical mutations, 'which is about a similar size patient population.'
quarterly_data.figure: Tagrisso $1.9B (+6%); FLAURA2 ~three-quarters of the U.S. first-line combination segment

quarterly_data.signal: Calquence grew 16% in the quarter, 'generating more than $1 billion in revenue for the first time in a single quarter,' and Dave Fredrickson said it maintains its position as the leading BTK inhibitor in frontline CLL across major markets despite intense competition. Within the finite duration class, AMPLIFY continues to gain share in reimbursed markets with encouraging early signs in the U.S., where it is uniquely positioned as the only BTK inhibitor with both finite and treat-to-progression options; management sees AMPLIFY as a significant growth driver through the remainder of 2026, supported by the clear global trend towards adoption of finite duration treatments.
quarterly_data.figure: Calquence +16%; more than $1 billion in a single quarter for the first time

quarterly_data.signal: Imfinzi and Imjudo delivered growth of 25% in aggregate in the second quarter, with meaningful contributions from MATTERHORN in gastric cancer and ADRIATIC in lung. Susan Galbraith reported that the phase III VOLGA interim analysis in muscle-invasive bladder cancer, covering 'the 50% of patients who are not candidates for cisplatin,' showed Imfinzi in combination with enfortumab vedotin delivering statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in both event-free survival and overall survival, while the Imjudo-containing arm showed a statistically significant improvement in event-free survival with a favorable trend in overall survival. Positive NILE results also came this quarter, and VOLGA complements NIAGARA and the recently U.S.-approved POTOMAC indication in earlier-stage non-muscle-invasive disease.
quarterly_data.figure: Imfinzi and Imjudo +25% aggregate in Q2; VOLGA addresses the 50% of patients not candidates for cisplatin

quarterly_data.signal: Enhertu grew 31% in the quarter to reported revenues of $888 million, with growth across all regions reflecting sustained market leadership in the HER2-positive and HER2-low breast cancer indications in major markets plus increased adoption and additional launches in emerging markets. Dave Fredrickson cited encouraging early signs of adoption and growing awareness in the first-line DESTINY-Breast09 setting in the United States following its approval late last year, and said the recent simultaneous U.S. approvals of DESTINY-Breast05 and DESTINY-Breast11 in the curative setting will become increasingly important through the remainder of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Enhertu $888M (+31%)

quarterly_data.signal: Datroway revenues of $55 million in the second quarter showed growing demand in later-line EGFR-mutated lung cancer with increasing second-line utilization in the U.S., and the launch in triple-negative breast cancer for patients who are not candidates for immunotherapy is underway following the U.S. approval of TROPION-Breast02 earlier in the quarter. Susan Galbraith argued AstraZeneca has 'a best-in-class TROP2-based ADC based on the design, which is based on the stable linker,' pointing to the half-life of the molecule and a lower rate of bone marrow toxicity than ADCs with less stable linkers and more exposure to the free payload. Two phase III trials read out later this year in the post-TKI second-line setting - TROPION-Lung15 (Datroway alone and in combination with Tagrisso) and SAFFRON (Tagrisso combined with Orpathys in MET-driven resistance) - while TROPION-Lung14 aims to bring the Datroway plus Tagrisso combination into the first line.
quarterly_data.figure: Datroway $55M in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: CLARITY-Gastric01 trial detail and the wholly-owned ADC franchise. Susan Galbraith said the trial met its overall survival dual primary endpoint with a statistically significant and highly clinically meaningful improvement versus investigator's choice of therapy in patients treated with at least two prior therapies, that there was a trend to PFS benefit which did not meet statistical significance, and that the key secondary endpoint also showed a highly clinically meaningful overall survival benefit in patients treated with at least one prior line. 'Fewer than 20% of patients with advanced gastric cancer survive beyond one year.' Sone-Ve is the first phase III data from the wholly-owned ADC portfolio, the second AstraZeneca ADC to demonstrate an overall survival benefit in gastric cancer after Enhertu, and the third positive phase III readout in this tumor type in just two years following MATTERHORN and DESTINY-Gastric04. The first-line CLARITY-Gastric02 study has a PD-L1 greater than 1% cohort and a less than 1% cohort, combining Sone-Ve with capecitabine with or without Rilvegostomig or nivolumab, and CLDN18.2 is also expressed on some pancreatic and biliary tract cancers being explored in ongoing phase I.
quarterly_data.figure: fewer than 20% of patients with advanced gastric cancer survive beyond one year

quarterly_data.signal: Breast and prostate phase III design detail. On camizestrant, Susan Galbraith said SERENA-4 has 'a larger sample size, 1,370 patients enrolled compared to PERSEVERE,' is designed to enrich for endocrine sensitivity, and is anticipated to read out in the second half of this year; she described an overall tolerability profile with low rates of GI side effects and a very low discontinuation rate. CAMBRIA-1 is an extended adjuvant switch trial in intermediate-to-high-risk hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative patients who have completed two-five years of adjuvant endocrine therapy with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor, which she said selects for an endocrine-sensitive population and 'has a good probability of success.' For saruparib, EvoPAR-Prostate01 is in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer and is powered for both the HRRM and non-HRRM cohorts, taking the learnings from PROpel into an earlier line, with the EvoPAR-Breast opportunity alongside it.
quarterly_data.figure: SERENA-4: 1,370 patients enrolled, readout in the second half of this year; CAMBRIA-1 enrolls patients who completed two-five years of adjuvant endocrine therapy

quarterly_data.signal: BioPharmaceuticals second-quarter product performance. Ruud Dobber said respiratory and immunology total revenue grew by 11%, with the established biologics for severe asthma generating 'over $2 billion of in-market sales in the first half.' Fasenra grew 13% to $570 million on continued IL-5 class leadership and grew 75% in emerging markets thanks to its launch in China, where it entered the National Reimbursement Drug List at the start of the year. Tezspire grew by 45% to $390 million. Breztri grew 20% to $346 million, received its first approval for asthma this year in the United States and a positive CHMP recommendation for asthma in Europe last week. Symbicort revenues of $671 million were down 8% on U.S. price pressure from a new generic competitor entering the market. Saphnelo increased 24% to $209 million on share gains in the intravenous segment for SLE patients, with a new subcutaneous formulation now available in the U.S. and some European markets.
quarterly_data.figure: R&I revenue +11%; severe asthma biologics >$2B in-market H1; Fasenra $570M (+13%, EM +75%); Tezspire $390M (+45%); Breztri $346M (+20%); Symbicort $671M (-8%); Saphnelo $209M (+24%)

quarterly_data.signal: Farxiga loss of exclusivity and its lifecycle defense. Ruud Dobber said generic competition entered the U.S. at the start of the quarter and that this, along with loss of exclusivity in some other markets and VBP in China, 'saw Farxiga decline by 90% overall, resulting in $1.8 billion of revenue for the quarter.' Three fixed-dose combinations are in development: Zibo-Depa, in phase III and recruiting very fast in proteinuria CKD; Balci-Depa in heart failure patients with a low eGFR where mortality is normally twice that of a normal heart failure patient and where 'more than 12 million patients in the top eight markets are eligible for a treatment like this'; and baxdrostat in combination with dapagliflozin in chronic kidney disease and hypertension. Data for both fixed-dose combinations are expected in the first half of 2027, building on dapagliflozin, of which Dobber said '60 million patients are currently treated.'
quarterly_data.figure: Farxiga -90% to $1.8B revenue for the quarter; >12 million eligible patients in the top eight markets; 60 million patients currently treated with dapagliflozin; FDC data in H1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Baxfendy launch and the primary aldosteronism opportunity. Ruud Dobber said the U.S. approval and launch were secured in May and the company is building early market access through affordability programs, with commercial access expected to broaden over the next few quarters 'in anticipation of Medicare Part D reimbursements from 2028.' Sharon Barr said primary aldosteronism is the leading cause of secondary hypertension and 'could affect as many as 5%-10% of all hypertensives and up to 20% of resistant hypertension,' that relatively few of those patients are screened today because there has been no therapy to give them, and that AstraZeneca has 'the first approved aldosterone synthase inhibitor'; the primary aldosteronism study has accrued very rapidly and the company is accelerating that timeline.
quarterly_data.figure: primary aldosteronism could affect as many as 5%-10% of all hypertensives and up to 20% of resistant hypertension; Medicare Part D reimbursement from 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Respiratory pipeline. Sharon Barr said the highly clinically meaningful OBERON and TITANIA phase III results for tozorakimab in COPD will be presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress in September, describing a potential first and best-in-class asset, and Pascal Soriot said that as a result 'we have increased our peak revenue expectation to more than $5 billion' for a product very few people thought would work and to which AstraZeneca itself had assigned a low probability of success. Ruud Dobber attributed the result to a mechanism 'inhibiting the anti-inflammatory pathway, but equally the mucus pathway,' and said the company is 'making an early start on our launch preparations for tezepelumab' (as spoken while describing the OBERON and TITANIA COPD data). Elsewhere in respiratory, the inhaled TSLP Sunakiment, formerly referred to as AZD8630, read out its phase II study with phase III plans under discussion with partner Amgen, and AstraZeneca entered an exclusive license agreement with CTTQ, a subsidiary of Sino Biopharmaceutical, for the development, manufacturing and commercialization of TQC3721, an inhaled small molecule PDE3/4 inhibitor already in phase III trials in China for COPD.
quarterly_data.figure: tozorakimab peak revenue expectation increased to more than $5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: The CARDIO-TTRansform miss and how it unwinds against the 2026 readout cohort. Sharon Barr said that in a contemporary ATTR cardiomyopathy population treated with standard of care, 'including 57% on a stabilizer,' adding Wainua did not provide a statistically significant benefit on the composite outcome of CV mortality and recurrent CV events; a pre-specified subgroup of patients on Wainua monotherapy showed fewer primary composite events, a nominally significant result, while no treatment effect was observed in patients on stabilizer therapy at baseline. AstraZeneca and Ionis will analyze the full data set and present at the European Society of Cardiology Congress in August. Aradhana Sarin said the $10 billion figure was 'the peak year estimates with the risk unwind' for the 2026 cohort, that some have unwound in a positive manner like Tozo and some not so positively like Wainua, and that 'I still think we'll unwind close to $10 billion' - not a 2030 number, since peak for some of these products may hit beyond 2030. Pascal Soriot added that AstraZeneca owns tozorakimab 100% whereas Wainua was to be shared with partner Ionis, so 'we gained more with Tozo than we lost with Wainua.'
quarterly_data.figure: 57% on a stabilizer in CARDIO-TTRansform; 2026 cohort still expected to unwind close to $10 billion in peak year sales

quarterly_data.signal: Cardiometabolic pipeline. Sharon Barr said the phase II-B VISTA trial of the oral GLP-1 elecoglipron showed 'a clinically meaningful and statistically significant weight loss of up to 11.8% at week 36, importantly, without evidence of a plateau,' while SOLSTICE showed 'an up to 1.9% reduction in HbA1c at week 26,' with a favorable safety profile and low discontinuation rates. First subject in was achieved for both EMBOLD (monotherapy in obesity or overweight) and ILLUMINATE (five phase III trials in Type 2 diabetes, as monotherapy and in combination with dapagliflozin), and ELEVATE is planned in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease; Pascal Soriot said 'we have now initiated five phase III trials for elecoglipron.' Beyond GLP-1, the phase II APRICUS trial of the selective amylin receptor agonist AZD6234 read out this quarter with a phase III monotherapy trial now initiating and data to be shared at EASD; the oral PCSK9 lariprostat has a phase III readout in the first half of 2027 with a first fixed-dose combination of lariprostat with rosuvastatin advancing into phase III, and Soriot said a further fixed-dose combination with elecoglipron is being developed. Ruud Dobber said the competitor's official first U.S. list price 'will not change dramatically our own outlook.'
quarterly_data.figure: VISTA weight loss up to 11.8% at week 36; SOLSTICE up to 1.9% HbA1c reduction at week 26; five phase III trials initiated for elecoglipron; oral PCSK9 phase III readout in H1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Rare Disease medicine-level performance. Marc Dunoyer said second-quarter Ultomiris grew 12% on patient demand across indications including the competitive MG and PNH markets, while Soliris revenues continued to decline due to successful conversion to Ultomiris as well as biosimilar pressure. Strensiq grew 36% year-on-year and 'remains one of AstraZeneca's fastest-growing blockbuster medicines,' supported by ongoing investment in commercial capabilities, infrastructure and disease awareness that also lays the foundation for the potential launch of efzimfotase alfa. Vosoritide continued to deliver strong global momentum, supported by expansion in adult patients with NF1-PN and uptake of the granule formulation in recently launched markets, and remained the market leader for pediatric patients with NF1-PN.
quarterly_data.figure: Ultomiris +12%; Strensiq +36%

quarterly_data.signal: Complement franchise pipeline. Marc Dunoyer said phase III I CAN data for Ultomiris in IgA nephropathy showed 'a 43% reduction in proteinuria, with significant proteinuria reduction seen as early as 10 weeks,' consistent across patient groups including those at higher risk of progression, and the company has now filed in both the U.S. and Japan. In HSCT-TMA, Ultomiris 'did not achieve statistical significance for the primary endpoint of event-free survival through 26 weeks compared to placebo in adults and adolescents aged 12 years older,' though it showed a trend towards treatment benefit; in pediatric patients AstraZeneca is advancing regulatory filings based on the open-label phase III trial reported in 2025 and data from an external control study. Asked about longer-acting C5 competitors, Dunoyer said the franchise continues to grow and the response is to pioneer new indications - IgAN, HSCT-TMA, delayed graft function and other renal rare diseases - and to develop other nodes of complement biology beyond C5.
quarterly_data.figure: I CAN: 43% reduction in proteinuria, significant reduction as early as 10 weeks; HSCT-TMA primary endpoint of event-free survival through 26 weeks not met

quarterly_data.signal: efzimfotase alfa in hypophosphatasia. Marc Dunoyer said the phase III pediatric MULBERRY and CHESTNUT data were presented at the International Conference on Children's Bone Health in June, and that in a pooled analysis of the phase III MULBERRY and HICKORY trials including pediatric, adolescent and adult patients, treatment 'resulted in a median of 361 days per year free from injection site reactions,' with injection site reaction rates 'five times lower than with Strensiq'; HICKORY data will be presented at the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research in October. In Q&A he said the filings 'will be above two years of age for a broad population,' done in discussion with regulatory authorities, covering adults with pediatric onset (already obtained in several countries with Strensiq) and adults with adult onset (where Strensiq is not approved today), and that 'even if we get less than the totality of the label that we have filed for, we expect to be within the range of $3 billion-$5 billion.' He contrasted dosing every two weeks against daily or every-other-day Strensiq and said patients on efzimfotase alfa have 'five days of injection site reaction on average in a given year,' which should improve country coverage, label breadth and patient retention.
quarterly_data.figure: median of 361 days per year free from injection site reactions; ISR rates five times lower than Strensiq; five days of ISR on average per year; filings above two years of age; peak sales within $3 billion-$5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Other Rare Disease programs. Marc Dunoyer said phase III CALYPSO data presented in May at ECE showed eneboparatide maintaining serum calcium within the target range, normalizing urinary calcium and restoring normal bone turnover in patients with hypoparathyroidism. For anselamimab in kappa light chain amyloidosis, results from the CARES program 'demonstrated a 62% reduction in all-cause mortality and a 71% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalization,' with an overall survival benefit observed even in patients with advanced Mayo stage disease. On the TTR depleter cliramitug, he said the trial is run 'as an add-on to either stabilizer, tafamidis or acoramidis, and Silences' and not as a monotherapy, that depletion of amyloid burden in the tissues was confirmed during phase I-B studies over one year, and that anselamimab provides a read-across for the depleter mechanism in amyloidosis; Pascal Soriot added that cliramitug can be used as monotherapy, on top of vutrisiran, or on top of stabilizers.
quarterly_data.figure: anselamimab CARES: 62% reduction in all-cause mortality and 71% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalization

quarterly_data.signal: Post-2030 growth platforms and the probability-of-success assumption behind the plan. Pascal Soriot said three recent launches - Datverzo, Etcamah and Baxfendy - each carry 'peak year revenue potential of more than $5 billion.' In next-generation IO, 'we now have 16 phase III trials across eight tumor types, including five in combination with our ADCs,' supporting an ambition to replace the current generation of checkpoint inhibitors. AZD0120 and surovatamig each have multiple phase III trials underway across hematology and both have now extended into autoimmune diseases, alongside investment in off-the-shelf and in vivo cell therapies. In ADCs and radioconjugates, phase III data for the second wholly-owned ADC Puxi-Sam are anticipated next year and first phase III trials for tovusam and zagaru were dosed this quarter. On the assumptions, Soriot said 'the average probability of success across phase III for the industry is 60%-65%,' that the aggregate probability of success AstraZeneca uses across its pipeline 'is around 60%,' and that '75%+ has been our record.'
quarterly_data.figure: Datverzo, Etcamah and Baxfendy each with peak year revenue potential of more than $5 billion; 16 phase III IO trials across eight tumor types including five with ADCs; industry phase III PTS 60%-65% vs around 60% assumed and a 75%+ record

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing environment and legal. Dave Fredrickson said AstraZeneca does not give brand-specific pricing commentary on most favored nation pricing, but that 'our pricing approach across all of launches now has really evolved in response to MFN,' and with 'the U.S. now referencing a basket of countries and setting its price, we are seeing productive engagement with payers in the wealthy nations within that context.' For Etcamah specifically, early negotiations are reflecting a new reality 'that funding for innovation needs to rise in line with a country's GDP per capita,' those discussions are expected to take more time than in the past, and the U.S. objective of prices in wealthy nations coming up and U.S. prices coming down a bit is 'the direction of travel.' Separately, Ruud Dobber confirmed that as noted in the legal disclosures the company 'started an arbitration process regarding Beyfortus in the United States' and does not comment on arbitration or legal procedures.

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Perioperative Imfinzi plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin (09-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AstraZeneca's supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for Imfinzi (durvalumab) in combination with enfortumab vedotin (EV) was accepted and granted Priority Review by the US FDA for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are ineligible for or have declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy. The PDUFA date is anticipated during the fourth quarter of 2026. The sBLA rests on the VOLGA Phase III trial (695 patients randomised 1:1:1, conducted in 182 centres across 25 countries), whose planned interim analysis showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in event-free survival and overall survival versus radical cystectomy with or without approved adjuvant treatment; the results will be presented at a forthcoming medical meeting. Regulatory applications based on VOLGA are under review in the EU, Japan and several other countries. Imfinzi is already approved in over 50 countries for cisplatin-eligible MIBC (NIAGARA), and more than 470,000 patients have been treated with Imfinzi since its first approval in May 2017. Susan Galbraith (EVP, Oncology Haematology R&D) said that, if approved, this would be the first perioperative regimen with enfortumab vedotin given only before surgery (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: US Priority Review; PDUFA anticipated during the fourth quarter of 2026; VOLGA 695 patients, 182 centres, 25 countries; Imfinzi approved in over 50 countries for cisplatin-eligible MIBC; more than 470,000 patients treated

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Trixeo approved in the EU for the maintenance treatment of (09-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The European Commission approved Trixeo Aerosphere (budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol fumarate dihydrate; marketed as Breztri Aerosphere in the US, China and Japan) as a maintenance treatment for asthma in patients 12 years of age and older not adequately controlled by a medium dose ICS/LABA combination, following the positive CHMP opinion. The approval is based on the KALOS and LOGOS Phase III trials (approximately 4,300 randomised patients), in which Trixeo showed statistically significant improvements in lung function versus combined ICS/LABA comparators and, in the pooled analysis, a statistically significant reduction in the annualised rate of severe asthma exacerbations; no new safety or tolerability signals were identified. Trixeo/Breztri is now approved for asthma in the US, Europe and Japan and is under review in China and other countries; it is also approved for COPD in more than 90 countries and was prescribed to more than 6.8 million patients globally in 2025. The company says Trixeo is the first and only triple-combination therapy approved in the EU for patients 12 years and older, independent of exacerbation history (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: EU approval for asthma (12 years and older); KALOS/LOGOS approximately 4,300 patients; COPD approved in more than 90 countries; prescribed to more than 6.8 million patients in 2025

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Klygefa (gefurulimab) recommended for approval in the EU by (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP issued a positive opinion recommending EU approval of Alexion's Klygefa (gefurulimab) as an add-on to standard therapy for adults with anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive generalised myasthenia gravis (gMG), with once-weekly subcutaneous self-administration via autoinjector. The opinion is based on the PREVAIL Phase III trial (260 patients from 20 countries), which met its primary endpoint: improvement from baseline in MG-ADL total score at week 26 versus placebo (treatment difference: -1.6 [95% CI: -2.4, -0.8], p<0.0001), with a clinically meaningful improvement as early as week one sustained through week 26; the safety profile was consistent with C5 inhibitors eculizumab and ravulizumab. Klygefa is already approved in Japan and other countries; submissions based on PREVAIL are under review in the US, China and additional countries. The company estimates 82,500 people are diagnosed with gMG in the EU5, 66,000 of them AChR-positive. The company says that, if approved, Klygefa will be the first and only dual-binding nanobody C5 inhibitor for this population (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion; PREVAIL MG-ADL treatment difference -1.6 (95% CI -2.4, -0.8), p<0.0001, 260 patients; 82,500 diagnosed in EU5, 66,000 AChR-positive

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Enhertu recommended for approval in the EU by CHMP as (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP recommended EU approval of AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) as monotherapy for the adjuvant treatment of adults with resected HER2-positive breast cancer who have residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane-based and HER2-targeted treatment. The opinion is based on the DESTINY-Breast05 Phase III trial (1,635 patients), in which Enhertu reduced the risk of invasive disease recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 (hazard ratio 0.47; 95% CI 0.34-0.66, p<0.0001); at three years 92.4% of Enhertu patients were alive and free of invasive disease versus 83.7% on T-DM1, with no new safety concerns. This indication is already approved in the US, Brazil, India and Canada. Enhertu was discovered by Daiichi Sankyo and is jointly developed and commercialised by AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo (collaboration since March 2019; Daiichi Sankyo keeps exclusive rights in Japan and is responsible for the manufacturing and supply of Enhertu and Datroway).
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion; DESTINY-Breast05 IDFS risk reduction 53% vs T-DM1 (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.34-0.66); 3-year IDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%; 1,635 patients

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Efzimfotase alfa granted Priority Review in the US as (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The US FDA accepted Alexion's Biologics License Application (BLA) for efzimfotase alfa (ALXN1850) and granted it Priority Review for patients with hypophosphatasia (HPP) aged 2 years and older; the PDUFA date is anticipated during the first half of 2027. The BLA is based on the three-trial Phase III programme: HICKORY (124 patients aged 12 and older, Strensiq-naive), MULBERRY (29 children aged 2 to <12, Strensiq-naive) and CHESTNUT (43 children previously treated with Strensiq); efzimfotase alfa showed a favourable safety profile and was generally well-tolerated across all three. HICKORY results will be presented at the 2026 ASBMR Annual Meeting. Regulatory submissions are also under review in Japan and other markets. The company estimates the addressable HPP population at 13,800 across the US, Germany, France, UK, Italy, Spain, Japan and China. The company says that, if approved, efzimfotase alfa will be the first treatment to address skeletal abnormalities and functional impairments regardless of disease onset, with dosing every two weeks (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: US Priority Review; PDUFA anticipated during the first half of 2027; HICKORY 124, MULBERRY 29, CHESTNUT 43 patients; addressable HPP population 13,800

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Alexion advances pioneering leadership in gMG care with (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Alexion will have 15 presentations in generalised myasthenia gravis (gMG) at the AANEM Annual Meeting and MGFA Scientific Session (29 September to 2 October 2026), led by new 52-week open-label extension data from the PREVAIL Phase III trial of gefurulimab. Patients on gefurulimab maintained clinical improvements through the extension (least squares mean, 95% CI: MG-ADL -5.3 (-5.8, -4.8); QMG -5.3 (-6.0, -4.6); MGC -9.4 (-10.3, -8.5)); patients who switched from placebo at week 26 improved from the first assessments and sustained it through week 52 (MG-ADL -4.9 (-5.4, -4.4); QMG -4.6 (-5.4, -3.9); MGC -8.3 (-9.2, -7.3)). Gefurulimab was well-tolerated and no meningococcal infections were reported. A separate PREVAIL analysis to be presented shows reduced risks of gMG-related hospitalisations and rescue therapy use with gefurulimab at week 26 versus placebo.
quarterly_data.figure: 15 presentations; PREVAIL 52-week OLE LS mean MG-ADL -5.3, QMG -5.3, MGC -9.4; placebo-switch MG-ADL -4.9, QMG -4.6, MGC -8.3; no meningococcal infections

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: AstraZeneca completes global license agreement for oral (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AstraZeneca completed its exclusive license agreement with Dizal Pharmaceutical for Zegfrovy (sunvozertinib), an oral irreversible EGFR inhibitor, acquiring worldwide rights to develop and commercialise it. Zegfrovy is approved in the US and China for 2nd-line NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations and is already available in China; AstraZeneca will launch it in the US during the fourth quarter of 2026. A 1st-line sNDA has been accepted by the US FDA and submitted to China's CDE (Breakthrough Therapy Designation in both). AstraZeneca says the transaction does not impact its 2026 financial guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: US launch in the fourth quarter of 2026; no impact on 2026 financial guidance

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Datroway approved in the EU as only TROP2-directed medicine (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The European Commission approved AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Datroway (datopotamab deruxtecan) as monotherapy for the 1st-line treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) who are not candidates for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy, following the positive CHMP opinion; Datroway is now approved for two breast cancer indications in the EU. The approval is based on the TROPION-Breast02 Phase III trial (644 patients): median overall survival 23.7 months versus 18.7 months with chemotherapy (a 5.0-month improvement; HR 0.79), a 43% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.57), and an objective response rate of 62.5% versus 29.3%. Datroway was approved in the US in May 2026 for the same indication; reviews are underway in China and Japan, and in Australia, Canada, Singapore and Switzerland under Project Orbis. It is approved in more than 30 countries/regions for this TNBC indication and in more than 45 for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. EVP Dave Fredrickson: more than 80,000 people in Europe are diagnosed with TNBC every year. Daiichi Sankyo's Ken Keller: Datroway is the only TROP2-directed ADC approved in the EU with an overall survival benefit in 1st-line metastatic TNBC (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: EU (EC) approval, 1st-line metastatic TNBC not eligible for immunotherapy; TROPION-Breast02 median OS 23.7 vs 18.7 months (HR 0.79), PFS risk reduced 43% (HR 0.57), ORR 62.5% vs 29.3%, 644 patients; US approval May 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Enhertu plus pertuzumab approved in the EU as first new (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The European Commission approved AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) in combination with pertuzumab for the 1st-line treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, following the positive CHMP opinion. The approval is based on the DESTINY-Breast09 Phase III trial (1,157 patients), in which the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 44% versus THP (taxane, trastuzumab and pertuzumab; hazard ratio 0.56), with median PFS of 40.7 months versus 26.9 months, and no new safety concerns. The company calls it the first new 1st-line regimen in more than a decade (company claim). Daiichi Sankyo's Ken Keller: this is the second new Enhertu indication in the EU in two months, following the recent tumour-agnostic approval. Enhertu plus pertuzumab is now approved in more than 40 countries/regions for this indication. Sales of Enhertu in most EU territories are recognised by Daiichi Sankyo.
quarterly_data.figure: EU (EC) approval, 1st-line HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer; DESTINY-Breast09 risk reduced 44% vs THP (HR 0.56), median PFS 40.7 vs 26.9 months, 1,157 patients; approved in more than 40 countries/regions

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Etcamah in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor approved in (09-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to Etcamah (camizestrant), a once-daily oral next-generation SERD, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib or ribociclib) for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer upon detection of an ESR1 mutation during aromatase inhibitor (AI) and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, based on an FDA-authorised test; concurrently the FDA approved a companion diagnostic test that detects emerging ESR1 mutations in circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA). The approval rests on the SERENA-6 Phase III trial (315 patients): the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 56% versus an AI plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor (HR 0.44; median PFS 16.0 versus 9.2 months), a later pre-planned analysis showed a PFS2 benefit of 25.7 versus 19.1 months (HR 0.63), and overall survival is still maturing. Recommended dose is 75mg with a CDK4/6 inhibitor. EVP Oncology Haematology Dave Fredrickson: this is the tenth FDA approval this year across AstraZeneca's portfolio and the fourth in breast cancer; the company calls it the first and only medicine of its type in the 1st-line setting (company claim). The company cites approximately 37,000 US patients with HR-positive metastatic breast cancer treated with a medicine in the 1st-line setting, approximately 30% of whom develop ESR1 mutations during 1st-line treatment before progression. Etcamah is also approved in more than 30 countries, including the EU, Japan, Canada and the UK.
quarterly_data.figure: US accelerated approval with companion ctDNA test; SERENA-6 progression-or-death risk reduced 56% (HR 0.44), median PFS 16.0 vs 9.2 months, PFS2 25.7 vs 19.1 months; tenth FDA approval of the year, fourth in breast cancer; approved in more than 30 countries

quarterly_data.signal: The ZEUS cardiovascular outcomes trial of ziltivekimab, with more than 6,300 people enrolled, failed to reduce MACE with a hazard ratio of 0.99 despite confirmed target engagement and reductions in free IL-6 and hsCRP. Martin Holst Lange framed it as a biomarker-causality test: 'There was a question on the correlation between the biomarkers and the actual outcomes, and that was the leap of faith that had to be tested.' For zenagamtide, an extra titration step was added and management said that 'from a modeling perspective, feel quite confident that we'll see a safety tolerability profile in line with what we've seen with, for example, CagriSema.'

quarterly_data.figure: IO GLP-1 sales +13%; IO obesity franchise +37%; around 58% GLP-1 volume market share outside the U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: Ozempic and the high-dose rollout outside the U.S. Emil Kongshoj Larsen said Ozempic 'continues to see solid sales momentum, with sales growth of 10% in the second quarter,' partially driven by Ozempic 2.0 mg, now launched in around 10 countries with good uptake, plus strong Ozempic performance across key European markets. Wegovy 7.2 mg in a single-dose pen is now broadly available in the U.K., where GLP-1 market share has increased since the step-up data, and the 7.2 mg single-dose pen was recently approved in the EU with the first EU market launches planned during Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: Ozempic sales growth 10% in Q2; Ozempic 2.0 mg launched in around 10 countries; Wegovy 7.2 mg single-dose pen EU launches in Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Semaglutide loss of exclusivity has begun. Emil Kongshoj Larsen said 'we saw the first generic entries in the early LOE markets. While modest so far, the LOE impact is expected to be back-end loaded in the second half of 2026.' Karsten Munk Knudsen identified those markets as Canada and Brazil mainly. Novo sees the market expanding in the early LOE countries, driven by more products available at lower prices and significant promotional investments by new entrants, and although generic players have started to capture market share, Novo has so far been able to grow its absolute volumes. In Canada the leading tactic is the savings card program, with good volume retention for both Ozempic and Wegovy in the cash and private insurance channels.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Wegovy pill rollout outside the U.S. Emil Kongshoj Larsen framed the U.K. headroom: it is estimated that around 20 million adults live with obesity in the U.K. while only around 1.6 million people were treated with obesity medication prior to launch, and 'almost three out of 10 obesity patients on a once weekly GLP-1 and IO live in the U.K.' He attributed the pent-up demand to a real injection barrier and to the pill's lack of drug-drug interactions, which lets patients on oral contraceptives and statins start easily. In the U.A.E. the Wegovy pill became available in early June, roughly one month after an oral competitor entered, and has already captured around 50% market share in the oral segment. Germany follows in September: a different, telehealth-driven market where more than half of the growth and a third of the market is already sold through telehealth channels.
quarterly_data.figure: U.K. around 20 million adults with obesity vs around 1.6 million treated; almost three out of 10 IO once-weekly obesity patients are in the U.K.; U.A.E. around 50% oral-segment share; Germany telehealth is more than half of growth and a third of the market

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Karsten Munk Knudsen walked the balance-of-year and 2027 run-rate bridge. First-half growth was 2%; from that run rate, factor in the loss of exclusivity for semaglutide in a few markets, Canada and Brazil mainly, which happens predominantly in the second half, and the favorable gross-to-net effects of a combined DKK 5 billion booked in Q3 and Q4 last year. The comparative effect does not carry forward into next year while the loss-of-exclusivity impact will annualize into it. On 2027 he declined to guide before February but noted 'the GLP-1 market is growing close to 40%, when we look at moving annual totals' and called out CagriSema's U.S. regulatory action and Mim8's regulatory decision as the swing factors.
quarterly_data.figure: first-half growth 2%; combined DKK 5 billion of favorable prior-year gross-to-net in Q3 and Q4; GLP-1 market growing close to 40% on moving annual totals

quarterly_data.signal: U.S. price and channel mix. Jamey Millar broke down the prior-period gross-to-net adjustment: of the DKK 2 billion highlighted, 'about 3/4 of the impact is Ozempic gross to net, and then the balance is insulin.' On Wegovy injectable he said Novo saw volume growth offset by lower realized prices than anticipated, with no new price dynamic impacting it - 'it's the price dynamic that we started the year with.' Karsten Munk Knudsen added that the business mix has changed: self-pay is now to the tune of 35% of total Wegovy injectable in the U.S., compared to a year ago when it was around the 10%-15% range, at a different price point but a good way to unlock volume.
quarterly_data.figure: DKK 2 billion gross-to-net adjustment, about 3/4 Ozempic and the balance insulin; Wegovy injectable U.S. self-pay around 35% of total vs the 10%-15% range a year ago

quarterly_data.signal: API capacity. Asked where the new API manufacturing facilities stand, Karsten Munk Knudsen said Novo has 'validated the first product in the first finger in the first facility' and that it is progressing very nicely, but that in terms of commercial supply into the marketplace there is 'very low utilization from these facilities, which makes us also bullish in terms of being able to supply significant volumes in the years to come, especially for the Wegovy pill for ex-U.S. rollout.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: REIMAGINE 4 head-to-head readout. CSO Martin Holst Lange said the completed open-label trial of CagriSema 2.4 mg versus tirzepatide 15 mg produced a weight loss of 15.2% and an HbA1c of 1.9 percentage points at 68 weeks; on the dual primary endpoint CagriSema demonstrated non-inferiority versus tirzepatide for weight reduction but not for HbA1c reduction. He defended the positioning by noting that across the CagriSema diabetes trials HbA1c lowering has run between -1.8% and 2.3%, alongside an 'almost unprecedented 15% weight loss' in diabetes and a 23% weight loss in obesity, plus benefits on blood pressure, glycemic control, lipids and potential bone preservation from amylin biology.
quarterly_data.figure: REIMAGINE 4: 15.2% weight loss and HbA1c of 1.9 percentage points at 68 weeks vs tirzepatide 15 mg; CagriSema diabetes HbA1c lowering between -1.8% and 2.3%; 23% weight loss in obesity

quarterly_data.signal: CagriSema dose-range program. Martin Holst Lange said Novo completed REDEFINE 9, a 68-week efficacy and safety trial testing CagriSema maintenance doses of 1.0 mg and 1.7 mg of each component in people with overweight obesity, where both lower doses achieved superior weight loss compared to placebo and CagriSema appeared safe and well-tolerated; detailed data come later this year. Novo also initiated the CagriSema phase III-B REDEFINE high-dose trial of 2.4 mg cagrilintide plus 7.2 mg semaglutide, comprising two substudies - obesity without diabetes, and obesity with type 2 diabetes - each measured against CagriSema 2.4 mg of each component and semaglutide 7.2 mg alone. He pointed to REDEFINE 11 as the trial testing individualized titration and dosing.
quarterly_data.figure: REDEFINE 9: 68 weeks, CagriSema 1.0 mg and 1.7 mg maintenance doses, superior weight loss vs placebo; REDEFINE high dose: 2.4 mg cagrilintide plus 7.2 mg semaglutide in two substudies

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline initiations beyond CagriSema. Martin Holst Lange said Novo initiated a phase II trial of its triple agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP and amylin receptors, evaluating different dose escalation regimens for up to 39 weeks and expected to read out in the second half of 2027, plus a phase II trial of once-weekly UBT251 in type 2 diabetes for up to 40 weeks expected to read out by the end of 2027. Planned starts include oral zenagamtide in obesity, cagrilintide high dose, AMBITION - the phase III development program for zenagamtide - and REIMAGINE SWITCH, which evaluates switching from semaglutide 1.0 mg and 2.0 mg to CagriSema with results anticipated in the second half of 2027. Phase III safety results from the SYNCHRONY Real-World trial of efruxifermin in people with MASH and fibrosis stages F1 to F4 are anticipated in the remainder of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: triple agonist phase II up to 39 weeks, readout second half of 2027; UBT251 phase II up to 40 weeks, readout by end of 2027; REIMAGINE SWITCH results second half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Oral franchise strategy. Martin Holst Lange said the completed 50 mg oral semaglutide study 'showed some really good results on both efficacy and tolerability,' but 'at this point in time, we do not see a need to launch the 50 mg' because with the approved 25 mg 'we come out with 17% weight loss and the best tolerability profile as far as we can see in the oral space,' and because Novo has oral zenagamtide plus three more oral assets in its current pipeline and portfolio. On zenagamtide he noted phase II showed 24% weight loss in a matter of six months treatment in obesity, and that it will be offered as both a subcutaneous injection and an oral, taking a further step up in efficacy for oral treatment.
quarterly_data.figure: oral semaglutide 25 mg: 17% weight loss; zenagamtide phase II: 24% weight loss in six months; three more oral assets in the pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: ZEUS safety detail and what happens to the inflammation strategy. Martin Holst Lange said the trial randomized patients in a 1:1 ratio to once-monthly ziltivekimab 15 mg or placebo on top of standard of care, with eligibility requiring high-sensitivity C-reactive protein equal to or above 2 mg per liter. Overall rates of adverse events and serious adverse events were similar between arms, but consistent with targeting IL-6 inhibition a higher proportion of ziltivekimab-treated people had serious infections compared to placebo. He said Novo had 'communicated an effect size of around 50% or less because we acknowledge the risk,' argued the CANTOS trial's IL-1 beta result means inflammation in cardiovascular disease should still be addressed, and said Novo has an NLRP3 asset in phase I plus additional NLRP3 assets in its pre-clinical pipeline that it intends to progress.
quarterly_data.figure: ziltivekimab 15 mg once-monthly, 1:1 randomization, hsCRP equal to or above 2 mg per liter; effect size communicated at around 50% or less

quarterly_data.signal: Business development posture. Mike Doustdar said he does not measure ambition 'by the number or the size of the acquisition we make' and that Novo is focused on bolt-ons that complement internal R&D - 'I've also said we are in every data room' - while a transformative M&A would require Novo to be in a very different situation than it is today. On where he is hunting: Novo sees obesity as 'not a single disease, but multiple conditions with 1 billion people suffering from it differently,' first segmenting the population into injectable versus orals, then looking at adjacent biologies - amylin, GIP and glucagon - that Novo understands scientifically and can manufacture and commercialize the way it does today.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 billion people living with obesity

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo's CagriSema delivers superior weight loss versus (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Topline phase 3 results for once-weekly CagriSema (cagrilintide + semaglutide), highlighted at Novo's Capital Markets Day. REIMAGINE 5 (adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin, an SGLT2 inhibitor or both): CagriSema 1.0 mg/1.0 mg achieved superior weight loss of 12.4% vs 9.1% for tirzepatide 5 mg and non-inferior HbA1c reduction (1.71% vs 1.67%) at week 60. REDEFINE 9 (overweight or obesity): CagriSema 1.0 mg/1.0 mg delivered 21.0% weight reduction vs 2.0% for placebo at week 68, meeting the primary superiority endpoint. CagriSema was well tolerated overall in both trials. The U.S. NDA for CagriSema in weight management, filed in December 2025, has a decision expected in Q4 2026. Novo also presented first data in painful diabetic neuropathy in type 2 diabetes, with details to come later.
quarterly_data.figure: REIMAGINE 5: weight loss 12.4% vs 9.1% (tirzepatide 5 mg), HbA1c 1.71% vs 1.67% at week 60; REDEFINE 9: 21.0% vs 2.0% placebo at week 68; FDA decision expected Q4 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Highlights to be presented at Novo's Capital Markets Day (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: At its Capital Markets Day in London, Novo set strategic ambitions for 2030 (by 2030 from a 2026 baseline; the company states they are inherently uncertain and do not constitute its financial outlook or guidance): launch >5 multi-blockbusters by 2030 and deliver >150 bDKK risk-adjusted pipeline sales in 2035; enter or complete ≥ 5 Phase 3 programmes in obesity and diabetes and ≥ 5 in other therapy areas; deliver 2026-30 revenue CAGR in line with industry peers (Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca, Roche and others named); scale capacity to be able to serve 10x more people with obesity on oral GLP-1; serve >60m patients globally by 2030; maintain a broadly stable operating margin and an attractive dividend per share. The revenue and margin ambitions are based on adjusted metrics.
quarterly_data.figure: >5 multi-blockbusters by 2030; >150 bDKK pipeline sales in 2035; ≥ 5 + ≥ 5 Phase 3 programmes; capacity for 10x more oral GLP-1 obesity patients; >60m patients by 2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo's once-weekly Sogroya (somapacitan) receives positive (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP recommended once-weekly Sogroya (somapacitan) for children with idiopathic short stature (ISS) with persistent growth disturbance, based on the REAL8 trial (non-inferior to once-daily growth hormone on mean annualised height velocity at Week 52). This follows the May 2026 CHMP recommendation for short stature in children born small for gestational age and with Noonan Syndrome; a European Commission decision on marketing authorisation covering all three indications is expected later this year. ISS affects up to 3% of children worldwide. The company says that, if approved, Sogroya would be the first and only growth hormone treatment approved for ISS in the EU (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion for ISS; EC decision on three indications expected later this year; ISS up to 3% of children

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo: CHMP recommends EU approval of FREHEMGO (denecimig), (09-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP adopted a positive opinion recommending EU marketing authorisation for FREHEMGO (denecimig), a factor VIIIa mimetic bispecific antibody given under the skin as routine prophylaxis for haemophilia A with or without inhibitors in adults and children, with once-monthly, once-every-two-weeks and once-weekly dosing in a single-use pre-filled pen; the company calls it the first FVIIIa mimetic to offer these three dosing options (company claim). The opinion is based on the FRONTIER programme: in the pivotal FRONTIER 2 trial denecimig significantly reduced the annualised bleeding rate versus prior clotting-factor prophylaxis and on-demand treatment, FRONTIER 3 in children younger than 12 years was consistent, mean annualised bleeding rates were generally below 1 in the reported phase 3 population, and FRONTIER 5 found no new safety signals on direct switching from emicizumab. Novo expects to launch FREHEMGO in the first European countries in Q4 2026 and broadly across the EU starting early 2027. Denecimig was submitted to the US FDA (BLA) in September 2025. CEO Mike Doustdar called it a differentiated treatment option that can reduce treatment burden.
quarterly_data.figure: CHMP positive opinion; first European launches Q4 2026, broad EU launch from early 2027; mean annualised bleeding rate generally below 1; US BLA submitted September 2025

quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo and Hengrui Pharma enter exclusive license agreement (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Licensor Hengrui Pharma: Novo Nordisk entered a license agreement with Hengrui Pharma (600276.SH; 01276.HK) for HRS-1596, a phase 1-ready GLP-1 receptor and GIP receptor dual agonist with potential for once-weekly oral dosing. Novo obtains exclusive rights to develop, manufacture and commercialise HRS-1596 globally, excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. The agreement is subject to U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance and other customary closing conditions and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. CSO Martin Holst Lange: 'we are excited to add HRS-1596 to our growing pipeline and to explore its potential to raise the bar for convenience in the field.'
quarterly_data.figure: exclusive global rights excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan; expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory approvals listed in the H1 2026 financial report that the Q2 call did not detail: in July the European Medicines Agency (EMA) granted approval of Wegovy pill for the treatment of excess body weight and long-term weight management, with SELECT cardiovascular data in the label; the US FDA approved the Wegovy FlexTouch pen for semaglutide 2.4 mg in obesity, with launch expected in the second half of 2026; the US FDA and the EMA approved the manual prefilled syringe (mPFS) device for Wegovy 2.4 mg and for Ozempic 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 mg doses; Awiqli was approved in the US; and the CHMP gave a positive opinion for adding SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE (Ozempic 2.0 mg as an add-on to dose-reduced insulin glargine) to the EU Ozempic label.
quarterly_data.figure: EMA: Wegovy pill (July); FDA: Wegovy FlexTouch 2.4 mg pen, Awiqli; FDA and EMA: mPFS devices for Wegovy 2.4 mg and Ozempic 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 mg; CHMP positive opinion: Ozempic SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE label

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue increased 22% to $382.5 million in the first quarter lapping a fully integrated Ambry. quarterly_data.quarter: Tempus AI press release: Tempus Receives FDA Clearance for its AI Product Intended (08-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Tempus received 510(k) clearance from the U.S. FDA for Tempus ECG-PH, an AI-enabled software device that analyzes standard 12-lead electrocardiograms for signs associated with pulmonary hypertension (elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure, mPAP > 20 mmHg), for patients 40 years of age or older with cardiovascular symptoms and no known history of PH; it provides a binary output and is not intended as a stand-alone diagnostic tool. ECG-PH is the third FDA-cleared device in Tempus' cardiovascular portfolio, adding pulmonary hypertension to its FDA-cleared AI products for atrial fibrillation and low ejection fraction.
quarterly_data.figure: FDA 510(k) clearance for ECG-PH; third FDA-cleared device in the cardiovascular portfolio; mPAP > 20 mmHg; patients 40 years of age or older

quarterly_data.quarter: Tempus AI press release: Tempus Secures Up to $9.5 Million in ARPA-H ADVOCATE (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Tempus was selected by ARPA-H (the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services) to receive an award of up to $9.5 million under its ADVOCATE program to build an autonomous clinical AI agent for patients with heart failure, which the company calls the first of its kind (company claim); the funding supports product development and clinical validation of the AI system in a multi-center prospective study. The agent builds on Tempus' existing AI products, including the Olivia agentic patient concierge, Tempus Next care-gap software that has already screened over 2.7 million cardiology patients, and a portfolio of three FDA-cleared ECG-AI products.
quarterly_data.figure: award of up to $9.5 million; Tempus Next has screened over 2.7 million cardiology patients; three FDA-cleared ECG-AI products

quarterly_data.quarter: Tempus AI press release: Tempus Launches Effort to Build the Largest Multimodal (09-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Tempus announced an initiative to build a research platform containing 100,000 whole genomes linked to longitudinal clinical information over the next several years, which the company calls the first de-identified multimodal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) dataset built around disease populations and patient outcomes, optimized for AI-driven research (company claim); once complete, Tempus plans to expand the effort with the goal of reaching one million genomes. The WGS data will be integrated into Tempus' existing de-identified multimodal data environment and accessed through Tempus Lens, where researchers and model developers can build and validate AI models without moving datasets, with a computational system for pre-training and post-training workflows. Development is already underway; the initial dataset is available through Tempus' Early Adopter Program, additional members will be onboarded in waves, and general availability is planned for mid-2027. CEO Eric Lefkofsky: adding whole genome data linked to longitudinal outcomes 'makes that platform even more powerful and gives researchers a richer foundation to build AI models.'
quarterly_data.figure: 100,000 whole genomes over the next several years; long-term goal of one million genomes; general availability planned for mid-2027

ECG-MR becomes the fourth FDA-cleared Tempus ECG-AI product, spanning arrhythmia, heart function, pulmonary vascular and valvular disease. SVP of Cardiology Brandon Fornwalt: with the fourth FDA-cleared ECG-AI product, 'we're building a growing portfolio that can identify signals across numerous types of heart and vascular disease from the same ECG.'

quarterly_data.quarter: BillionToOne press release: Largest Prospective Study in General-Risk Pregnancies (08-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: BillionToOne announced publication in The Green Journal of a prospective, multi-site study of its cfDNA testing for recessive conditions in a general-risk pregnancy population, which the company calls the first prospective NIPT study in an intended-use screening population with near-complete pregnancy outcome ascertainment. Across nine U.S. institutions the study evaluated 2,212 pregnant carriers whose partner carrier status was unknown at testing, with cfDNA fetal risk results for cystic fibrosis, spinal muscular atrophy and alpha- and beta-hemoglobinopathies, and outcomes collected for 98.6% of pregnancies completing care at participating sites. Unity Fetal Risk Screen showed 94.4% sensitivity, 99.5% specificity and >99.9% negative predictive value, with consistent performance across a racially and ethnically diverse population; the company says traditional carrier screening alone classifies fewer than 50% of affected pregnancies as high-risk, mainly due to incomplete partner screening. The screen reports a personalized fetal risk as high as 9-in-10 (versus a maximum 1-in-4 from traditional screening when both partners are confirmed carriers) and as low as 1 in 10,000.

quarterly_data.signal: Caris Detect, a multi-cancer early detection blood test built on ultra-deep Whole Genome Sequencing together with cell-free RNA, launched in June 2026 and identifies 58 distinct cancer types from a single blood draw. quarterly_data.signal: The company published a study in npj Precision Oncology on the development and validation of Caris AI Insights for pancreatic cancer, an AI-based molecular signature that predicts first-line treatment benefit in advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, built on its clinico-genomic datasets across thousands of patients. In the testing cohort, standard molecular risk patients predicted to benefit from FOLFIRINOX achieved a median overall survival of 16.0 months when treated with FOLFIRINOX versus 9.9 months with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gem/nab-p); approximately half of the patients in the study received a different first-line therapy than the model would have recommended, which the company says highlights the potential opportunity for more biologically informed treatment selection to improve survival and reduce toxicity. The model gives clinicians a standard / high molecular risk stratification and guidance between FOLFIRINOX and gem/nab-p.
