quarterly_data.signal: The company announced publication in The Lancet Neurology of what it calls the first longitudinal cohort study to evaluate a broad panel of plasma biomarkers in patients receiving anti-amyloid antibody therapy (lecanemab) in real-world clinical practice. Led by Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis investigators, the study used Alamar's NULISAseq CNS 120 panel to measure 130 plasma proteins, profiling 2,385 samples from 1,967 participants with just 25 microliters of plasma per sample. Results stated by the company: proteins associated with amyloid clearance were largely different from those associated with subsequent cognitive decline; among 197 lecanemab-treated patients, 34 of the 130 biomarkers significantly changed with the number of infusions, not all in the same direction; and brain-derived forms of tau consistently outperformed the same proteins circulating in the periphery, accounting for four of the top five proteins distinguishing these patients from controls both before treatment and at the last infusion stage. The company says measuring these variants alongside more than 100 additional proteins in a single sample is what allowed the investigators to track pathology and treatment response in one assay. CEO: the study shows why measuring one or two biomarkers is not enough to understand treatment and why ultra-high sensitivity matters.

quarterly_data.signal: REC-4881 (FAP), CFO Ben Taylor: FAP patients undergo on average about 10 major surgeries and about 70 treatments with excisions over their lifetime. For the FDA discussions on pivotal design (described as productive), Recursion built an LLM model using over 250,000 patient records to study standard clinical practice and created a natural history database with a university in the Netherlands that tracked FAP patients over 20 years, showing continuous annual polyp growth averaging 'north of 50%'; he said Recursion would be fine even with the same trial design as the existing trial. Longer follow-up and data on managing known MEK1/2 side effects will be presented at the upcoming FAP physicians' conference, where Recursion presents at the presidential plenary.

quarterly_data.quarter: Absci press release: Absci Announces Preliminary Details for Phase 2 STORYLINE (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Absci announced additional details for its planned global, multi-center Phase 2 STORYLINE trial of ABS-201, an investigational anti-prolactin receptor (PRLR) antibody engineered with its generative AI platform, for endometriosis. The planned double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial would assess efficacy and safety in participants with surgically-diagnosed endometriosis and moderate to severe endometriosis-associated pain after a run-in period, with efficacy endpoints including reductions in dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain. Absci anticipates recruiting approximately 150 patients from approximately 10 or more countries, subject to protocol finalization and regulatory clearance, and anticipates initiation in mid-2027. It is designed as a dose-ranging trial, anticipating testing two or three dose levels to be confirmed following review of data from the ongoing HEADLINE trial.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 150 patients; approximately 10 or more countries; anticipated initiation mid-2027; two or three dose levels

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sean McClain: the ABS-201 pattern hair loss Phase II 13-week efficacy data will be announced in December of this year, with recruitment 'going extremely well'; the 26-week data are expected in early 2027. After the 26-week readout and safety data Absci plans to go to the FDA to begin registrational studies in 2027, while still collecting one-year post-dose durability data. He said roughly 1,500 patients will be needed for a safety database across all trials, and Absci internally estimates the per-patient trial cost at $60,000-$70,000.
quarterly_data.figure: 13-week data in December; 26-week data early 2027; roughly 1,500-patient safety database; $60,000-$70,000 per patient

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjiv Patel: lead asset zovegalisib, a PI3K-alpha mutant-selective inhibitor, is being developed in three indications. In second-line HR+/HER2- breast cancer, data at the pivotal 400 milligram BID dose showed 11 months of PFS versus 'the 5 and a half months of capivasertib'; a 1-to-1 randomized pivotal trial of fulvestrant plus zovegalisib versus fulvestrant plus capivasertib opened in mid-2025 (President of R&D Don Bergstrom), with precedent trials taking 30 to 36 months to fully enroll, and an update on expected last patient in comes at year end. quarterly_data.signal: First-line breast cancer: Relay chose a triplet of endocrine therapy plus Pfizer's selective CDK4 inhibitor atirmociclib plus zovegalisib for tolerability. quarterly_data.quarter: Ginkgo Bioworks press release: Ginkgo Datapoints and Apheris Welcome AbbVie, argenx, (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Ginkgo Datapoints and Apheris GmbH kicked off the Antibody Developability Consortium with founding members AbbVie, argenx, Lundbeck and Takeda; it remains open to additional pharmaceutical and biotech companies. Each founding member contributes proprietary antibody sequences, with Ginkgo Datapoints filling remaining capacity from public sources to reach 10,000 antibodies in total. Ginkgo Datapoints leads the scientific design and execution (sequence selection, antibody production, high-throughput wet-lab characterization across core developability endpoints) and trains a foundation antibody developability model on the dataset inside Apheris' secure environment; Apheris' federated infrastructure delivers the model into each member's environment for fine-tuning on proprietary molecules. The initial dataset is targeted for delivery to members by early 2027. Ginkgo calls it the field's largest standardized antibody developability dataset (company claim).
